🤖 Offline decode of the [September 15 missing-peer dump](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/441) narrows the stall to a self-deadlocked CTA inside QuACK 0.6.4's SM100 grouped GEMM, and identifies the one code path that separates the warps that retired from the warps that did not. QuACK is not exonerated: the rank stops inside this kernel with no external dependency left, and the deadlock is structural to its CLC scheduler. The initiating condition is still unproved, and two reproduction attempts at production shape did not trigger it.

The stuck kernel is the `dh` backward GEMM (`quack_grouped_gemm(dy, w2, cu, b_major="k")`, tile 256x256, cluster 2x2x1, CLC on). Both resident clusters show the same state in every CTA: the MMA warp and all four epilogue warps have exited, the TMA load warp waits on an A/B empty barrier that the exited MMA warp will never release, and the scheduler warp is still inside its CLC loop. The scheduler ring holds three valid grants (work indices 3996/4032/4068 in one cluster, 4011/4047/4083 in the other), and the ring's barrier words show every warp released grants 1-4 while only the four scheduler warps released grant 5. So the MMA and epilogue warps decoded grant 4 as "no more work" and retired, while the load and scheduler warps decoded the same grant as a valid batch-1 tile and kept going. The load warp's registers hold the batch-1 window `[2214, 4182)` (369 and 328 M-clusters for the first two groups), inside which index 4032 is valid; the retired warps must have used a window ending in `(4011, 4032]`. No invalid CLC response was ever in the ring, so this is not the spurious-cancel failure fixed in 0.6.4.

Every warp role decodes its own tile from `cu_seqlens` in global memory (`VarlenMTileScheduler._delinearize_work_idx`, with a per-warp cached batch window). Only the load and scheduler warps execute `griddepcontrol.wait` first (SASS `ACQBULK` at kernel offsets +2272 and +10528); the MMA and epilogue warps' `cu_seqlens` loads (+15408, +21696) come before any wait, and upstream main still has the same placement (`336a5ca` "Enable PDL"). The kernel is launched with PDL (`use_pdl=True` default) and the XLA fusion after it was already resident at its `ACQBULK`, so the sequence is PDL-chained. Under the hero's `save_moe` remat, `cu` is recomputed in the backward by a small fusion, so a predecessor that writes `cu` is plausible. That is the only per-role difference in the decode path and the natural explanation for a role-consistent split, but a one-time stale read at kernel start does not by itself produce the observed state: the retired warps rescan the window at later grants, and a fresh rescan resynchronizes them. The observed state requires those warps to keep seeing stale group boundaries for the whole kernel, which I could not reproduce.

Two probes on `cw-us-east-08a` (2 nodes, production priority, both clean, `/mwittmann/8870-quack-pdl-repro-2` and `/mwittmann/8870-quack-moe-bwd-probe-1`): (1) `experiments/grug/recovery/quack_pdl_repro.py`, the production `dh` GEMM at 601,088 rows with the routing alternating every launch so a stale decode is visibly wrong, six arms (production config, PDL off, CLC off, QuACK patched to wait in the MMA/epilogue warps, constant routing, and the `cu` writer as the immediate predecessor), 600 launches per GPU per arm on 8 GPUs, 28,800 launches, zero hangs and zero output mismatches; (2) `experiments/grug/recovery/quack_moe_bwd_probe.py`, the full `_expert_mlp_quack_wgrad` forward plus backward with a fresh random routing every iteration, 1,500 iterations per GPU on 8 GPUs, 72,000 GEMM launches, zero hangs, zero non-finite values. The hero rate is roughly one hang per 1e6 GPU-steps, about 3e-9 per GEMM launch, so a clean 1e5 launches neither confirms nor excludes the PDL path. In probe (1) the PDL-off arm ran at the same speed as production (27 ms versus 27 ms per launch), so disabling PDL on these launchers costs nothing measurable at this shape.

What this changes: the pooled-wave backend runs dense einsums and never touches this kernel, which matches its clean record. CLC off alone removes the per-grant decode (the scheduler warp decodes once and broadcasts) but leaves the initial-tile decode per warp, so it converts most of this failure into wrong or missing tiles rather than a hang, at the 5-12% GEMM cost recorded in `sonic_cute.py`. The cheap, targeted mitigation for the next hero restart is `use_pdl=False` on the three `quack_moe_cute` launchers (or the two-line wait in the MMA and epilogue warps, arm `patched`, to propose upstream); its efficacy can only be judged by the hang recurrence interval, currently one to two thousand steps.

🤖 Decoding the step-108711 dump (`/tmp/8870-watch-108711/`, task 90) the same way as the step-107501 one adds two facts that the earlier dump could not give, because this one has seven stuck clusters instead of two.

Six of the seven clusters split at a shared threshold. Their scheduler rings hold grants 4305-4404, the load and scheduler warps hold the fresh windows (group 1 is work indices `[2220, 4398)`, group 2 is `[4398, 6558)`; both are in the load warps' `R7/R8/R9` and the scheduler warps' `R8/R9`), and the ring barrier counts show which grant the MMA and epilogue warps retired on: 4358, 4363, 4365, 4340, 4362, 4367 after accepting 4324, 4328, 4332, 4305, 4327, 4333. The retired warps' end of work therefore sits in `(4333, 4340]` in all six clusters, one value, 58-64 indices short of the real end of group 1. That is one stale set of group boundaries shared by 24 CTAs on 24 SMs, not per-CTA noise.

The seventh cluster (blocks 12-13, initial work index 6) is stuck on its very first tile. Its load warp holds the fresh group-0 window `[0, 2220)` and has filled six A/B stages of tile 6 that were never consumed (A/B full parity 1, empty parity 0 in every stage), its scheduler ring holds one grant (index 13, released by the four scheduler warps only), and its MMA and epilogue warps are gone. The MMA warp exited before issuing a single MMA, so it decoded the initial tile, `idx 6 < 2220`, as no work. That is a decode from `cu_seqlens` that says the kernel has fewer than seven clusters of work, taken in the first microseconds of the kernel, by exactly the warps that do not execute `griddepcontrol.wait`. This case needs no persistence argument at all, which was the gap in the previous comment: a stale read at kernel start deadlocks the CTA on its first tile directly. The six other clusters show the same read at a slightly later moment, with `cu_seqlens[1]` already current and the later boundaries not, which fits a buffer being written while the non-waiting warps read it.

One correction to the earlier reading of the scheduler warps: they are parked at the CLC throttle `bar.sync` (kernel offset +11968) waiting for a load-warp credit that never comes, and the reported PC is the following `TRYWAIT`. With that, every barrier count in both dumps reconciles (loads on the tile the MMA warp abandoned, scheduler one credit ahead).

Taken together with the SASS (only the load and scheduler warps wait before their first `cu_seqlens` load), I now put the PDL-stale-input mechanism well above the alternatives. The `cu_seqlens` read the monitoring agent added to the capture is the confirming measurement: on the next hang, the buffer should hold the boundaries the load warp used (`[0, 2220)` and `[2220, 4398)` in work-index units are 370 and 363 M-clusters of 256 rows) while the retired warps evidently used a set that ended around 723 clusters in total. Independently of that read, `use_pdl=False` on the three `quack_moe_cute` launchers, or the two-line wait in the MMA and epilogue warps, is the change to trial at the next relaunch.

🤖 The September 18 UTC stall at step 118837 followed an InfiniBand port failure. Its RAS signature differs from the earlier GPU hangs; no CUDA debugger was attached. The automatic retry restored checkpoint 118722 and resumed training. [Incident record](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/470). Monitoring continues with the two-minute threshold and the updated capture ready.

🤖 The September 18 stall after step 120206 was another permanent-checkpoint metadata deletion failure. Checkpoint 120000’s pending `DeleteObjects: AccessDenied` surfaced at the next checkpoint synchronization. The automatic retry restored 120000 and resumed training, rolling back 206 steps. [Incident record](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/473). The metadata commit incompatibility remains; this event provides no GPU-state evidence of an 8870 recurrence. Monitoring continues on attempt 3.

🤖 The September 19 interruption after step 124715 began with `CUDA_ERROR_CONTAINED` on task 14, local GPU 3, followed by GPU-reset-required and NVLink-mask node conditions. The error leaves invalid peer-memory access versus hardware/driver fault unresolved. No RAS or debugger capture is available, so this does not confirm another silent #8870 hang. Iris automatically retried from checkpoint 124642; attempt 1 resumed and later passed 127172. Evidence and recovery: [incident record](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/488).

Permanent checkpoint 126000 subsequently logged successful completion with the deployed metadata fix, and later temporary checkpoints also completed. This verifies permanent publication; restoring 126000 has not been tested. [Checkpoint incident update](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/473). The 120-second no-progress monitor is rearmed on attempt 1 with the updated capture ready.

The strongest discriminator now seems to be CLC rather than ragged A2A itself. Since the captured CTAs show scheduler/load warps alive after MMA/epilogue exit, please treat the PDL-off run as a separate mechanism test: it does not by itself rule out CLC scheduling.

A useful production-geometry matrix would be: (1) current QuACK with CLC, (2) 0.6.4 drain fix with CLC, and (3) identical 0.6.4 build with CLC disabled. Keep the same checkpoint, rack map, and capture trigger. If only (3) survives comparable exposure, that materially localizes the failure; if (2) and (3) both survive, capture state from (1) remains essential to distinguish the fix from timing.

🤖 The September 23 stall on `hero-fa4sm100-nomask-step146k` was traced to rank 0 waiting in an S3 `put_object` for checkpoint 146585’s `manifest.json`. Two host-thread captures showed the same stack. NCCL reported only rank 0 behind, unlike the previously captured rack-wide GPU hangs; no CUDA debugger was attached. Why the S3 call remained blocked is unresolved.

The existing watchdog terminated the stalled attempt, and Iris automatically started attempt 1. All 176 tasks were running by 00:00:27 UTC September 24. The retry restored temporary checkpoint 146355 at 00:01:55, rolling back 228 steps from the last observed metric, then resumed training through step 146366. The two-minute monitor is rearmed. [Incident and evidence](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/518).

topics.body:

Version metadata and the optional Rust executable differ; equivalence of that executable is unproved. The normal Python serving and trainer paths leave it disabled.

The Snowball serving-mesh fix is merged in #9401. Retain the regression comparing logits from identical weights on the canonical training and serving meshes. Fresh normal-install HF-export parity passed all 64 representative cases with Levanter on 8 H100s and vLLM on 8 and 16 H100s. Maximum logged absolute probability differences from stored references were 0.056754, 0.064367 and 0.055632, respectively, within the unchanged 0.075 Levanter/0.125 vLLM bounds. Both vLLM configurations passed exact runtime placement/stage checks and exact same-rank token/logprob repeatability on a 15,025-token sentinel with fresh recomputes. Cross-rank variation is diagnostic. These application results cover the standalone Transformers 5.18.0 profile.

Earlier Snowball and Hero runs passed fresh training, checkpoint restoration and HF export on H100 and GB200 against the 47b wheels in MarinSkyRL's combined profile (Transformers 5.12.1). Hero/GB200's driver finished before a worker pod was deleted during shutdown; four queued worker retries were canceled. [MarinSkyRL #944](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/944) reconciles the exact released wheel pins at `cb2565d6`; all six current CI checks passed. Its explicit applicability assessment retains the original four-case evidence with its source/lock and sampling limits. New normal frozen combined installation and repeated Hero ShortConv/FP32-bias weight publication checks passed on H100 and GB200. The separate [native Snowball checkpoint failure](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9400#issuecomment-6129427326) covers a different path from this HF-export parity gate.

The frozen MarinSkyRL training and serving package set retains Transformer Engine 2.20.2 and its other agreed native dependencies. Follow-up Transformer Engine 2.19.0/2.20.2 repeats averaged 49.489/50.198 seconds over 18 warm updates per version, a descriptive 1.43% difference. Logical rank placement varied, and one process used a replacement allocation. The original cause and performance equivalence remain unproved. topics.title: mini-swe-agent sandbox contains clean copies of SWE-smith task repositories
topics.body:
When Harbor runs the mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 adapter on a SWE-smith task, the agent's own Python environment is installed inside the task sandbox at agent setup (`/root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/`). That environment contains clean, unbroken copies of three packages that are also SWE-smith task repositories: pygments, pandas and tenacity. The agent can read the fixed source directly. The same class exists at the image level, independent of the agent: conda's package cache ships boltons in every conda image, pip and setuptools vendor chardet, tomli and inflect, and one testbed environment holds an installed dataset egg.

Observed: in a GLM 5.3 trial on `swesmith-00763` (jd/tenacity) with the mini-swe-agent adapter, the agent ran `sed -n 136,175p /root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/tenacity/retry.py`, called it "the reference", copied the logic and passed. A pre-agent audit of the task packages cannot see this environment, because it appears only when the agent is installed.

Scope in the DCAgent SWE-smith packages (`DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s`), measured with mini-swe-agent's dependencies pinned (identical 80 distributions across one image per repository): pygments 222 tasks, pandas 196, tenacity 30, boltons 21, chardet 10, tomli 23, inflect 27, dataset 13. In the 2,100-task shootout pool that was 542 tasks before replacement. A filename-only check produces false positives (pygments' `html.py` versus safety, IPython's `timing.py` versus alive-progress), so the check must compare module contents or names, not file suffixes.

Reproduce: start a trial with the mini-swe-agent adapter on any pygments, pandas or tenacity SWE-smith task, and in the agent phase list `/root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/<package>/`. For the image-level copies, build the task's `environment/Dockerfile` and search outside `/testbed` for directories named after the task repository's import name (for example `find / -path /testbed -prune -o -type d -name tomli -print`).

Impact: pass rates on those tasks are inflated and the resulting traces teach reading a library copy instead of fixing the bug. Terminus-2 is not affected by the tool-environment copy, because the Terminus-2 agent runs outside the sandbox, but the image-level copies affect every agent. Existing SWE-smith trace sets were generated with other agent setups, so their tool environments may differ; they have not been audited for these paths.

Expected: during the agent phase, no readable copy of the task repository exists outside `/testbed`. Either the agent environment lives outside the sandbox (as Terminus-2 does), or the adapter installs it on a path the agent cannot read, or task packages whose repository is a dependency of the agent or of the base image are excluded from training pools and flagged in evaluation.

Done when: Harbor's mini-swe-agent adapter keeps its environment out of the agent's reach or documents the limitation; a content-based image check for repository copies outside `/testbed` is part of SWE-smith package validation; and existing SWE-smith trace sets are audited for reads under these paths. The shootout pool (#10213) already excludes the eight repositories above, pins the agent's dependencies, and drops traces that read a library copy of the task repository; the method and per-repository evidence are in the pool manifest at `open-athena/Snowball-SFT-Shootout-Pool-2026.10`. Related: #10212 (git history left in the same packages).

comments.body:
🤖

# Research

Harbor's Mini-SWE setup puts its Python tool environment inside the task container; a GLM 5.3 trial read the installed `tenacity/retry.py` and passed using that reference ([probe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10212#issuecomment-6227834962)). [Pool P v4](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10213#issuecomment-6228022768) excludes the affected repositories, and its row builder drops known library-copy reads, but those controls apply to this shootout rather than to future SWE-smith packages or older traces. Marin delegates agent execution to the pinned Harbor runtime, so the adapter, package validator, and trace audit need separate changes.

**Relevant code**
- [`trial_driver.py#L104-L116`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/trial_driver.py#L104-L116) — Harbor agent selection.
- [`driver_config.py#L69-L80`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/driver_config.py#L69-L80) — pinned external runtime.
- [`penfever_rollouts.py#L702-L708`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/penfever_rollouts.py#L702-L708) — one historical SWE-smith trace source.

# Proposal

Keep the v4 exclusions as the current safeguard. Add the following durable checks before treating other SWE-smith packages or historical traces as clean.

1. **Harbor adapter:** Move the Mini-SWE controller and its Python environment outside the task sandbox; send tool commands through Harbor's sandbox execution interface. Probe after agent setup, when the tool environment currently appears, and verify that the agent can edit `/testbed` but cannot read the controller's packages. If Harbor cannot support this boundary, document the limitation in the adapter and reject repository/agent pairs whose code ships in its pinned dependencies. The adapter change belongs in `marin-community/harbor`; Marin should pin the tested revision.
2. **Package validation:** Promote the [v4 image probe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10212#issuecomment-6228022644) into the SWE-smith package build gate. Inspect agent-readable files outside `/testbed` in the built image and again after agent setup. Use repository import names and distribution metadata to find candidates, then confirm source overlap with content fingerprints; a matching filename alone must not reject a task. Record matched paths, files, image revision, and agent dependency pin in the manifest, and reject confirmed overlaps before publishing packages.
3. **Historical traces:** Inventory each existing SWE-smith trace source and its agent/setup revision, starting with the registered Penfever source and the Kimi traces noted in [#10212](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10212#issuecomment-6228022644). Join commands and observations to the task repository; flag reads from its copies in `site-packages`, `_vendor`, conda caches, eggs, Go module caches, and agent tool environments. Publish counts and example paths by dataset and repository, quarantine confirmed contaminated rows, and mark sources with missing command or environment provenance as unknown rather than clean. Run the audit where the traces are stored to avoid bulk cross-region transfer.

## Testing and rollout

Test the validator against the observed tenacity tool environment and vendored tomli, plus unrelated files such as Pygments' `html.py`; the latter must not trigger on its filename. Run one Mini-SWE task end to end with the new boundary and verify that setup, editing, and the verifier still work. Hand-check flagged and unflagged audit samples, publish the audit manifest and rejected counts, then require the validator result in future SWE-smith pool manifests.

## Costs and open question

Moving the controller changes Harbor's agent lifecycle and needs an integration test, while scanning built images adds package-build work. Can Harbor's current Mini-SWE adapter run outside the sandbox with its existing command transport? If not, the documented limitation plus enforced repository exclusions is the immediate adapter deliverable; the package gate and trace audit remain required.

🤖 **TL;DR:** in the existing SWE-smith trace sets, clean copies outside `/testbed` matter little for the testbed-format tasks, and mini-swe-agent's tool env never appears. They ran Terminus-2, not mini-swe-agent. The exception is AgentTrove's clone-format tasks: 1,142 of their traces read an installed release copy of the task's own package.

| Set (revision) | Traces | Agent command reads a library copy of the task's repo | Touches mini-swe-agent's tool env | Row-builder drop (copy or tool env anywhere in the trace) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `open-athena/Kimi-2.5-swesmith-...-maxeps-32k` (`1b87a9cf78`) | 9,356 | 2 (1 of 5,237 passes) | 0 | 6 |
| `laion/calibforge-relay-traces` `kimi_swesmith` (`66feab4d24`) | 4,392 | 1 (0 passes) | 0 | 3 |
| `DCAgent2/GLM-4.7-swesmith-...-maxeps-131k` (`e209a88db1`) | 9,437 | 3 | 0 | 10 |
| `open-thoughts/AgentTrove` swesmith rows (`b395a4307a`) | 78,246 | 1,157 (1,142 in clone tasks) | 0 | 1,598 |

- **Clone tasks:** the instruction makes the agent clone `swesmith/<mirror>` into an image that already has the package installed. The agents then `ls` or `cat` the installed copy (`/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/<pkg>`, `/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/<pkg>`, a venv's `site-packages`), and that copy is clean code. 106 repos are affected; cantools, pygments, oauthlib and python-docx lead. The same tasks also expose the full mirror history (see #10212).
- **Go module cache:** 2 traces read a Go repo's module-cache copy. The shootout lists no import names for Go repos, so this column is supplementary.

**Method:** the shootout row builder's own rules, used verbatim: `LIBRARY_LOCATION` plus the repo's import names, and `AGENT_TOOL_ENV`. They are applied to the agent's commands, and also to the whole trace, matching the builder's drop rule. Import names are the shootout's for its 38 repos and extended for the rest. Code and exact regexes: [`scripts/task215/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/29a6fb1919/scripts/task215).

topics.title: [evaluation] Evalchemy c1d5c62c keeps a stale aggregate when rerun over a scored archive with transport-failure rows
topics.body:
Evalchemy at the policy pin `c1d5c62cdc3939b42f64411af44fd50716b53454` does not update an archive's results when a scored result already exists, even if that result contains transport-failure rows. A selective rerun that regenerates the failed rows therefore leaves the old aggregate and samples in place.

`write_finestore_output` returns before writing when `completed_finestore_output` is true ([`eval/contracts/finestore_output.py` L66](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/c1d5c62cdc3939b42f64411af44fd50716b53454/eval/contracts/finestore_output.py#L65-L67)). A result counts as completed when it is marked scored, and a result with failure markers is still marked scored.

Impact: on 2026-10-18 a GSM8K record had 112 `model_transport` failure rows out of 1,319. A selective rerun regenerated exactly those 112 units (1,207 retained resume payloads byte-identical), but the aggregate and samples stayed stale. Recovery required dropping the `evalchemy_results` and `samples` tables from a copy of the archive and rerunning the evaluator over the 1,319 cached responses (job `/karan/task204-gsm-ep2-cached-regrade-20261018`).

Reproduce:
1. Run Evalchemy GSM8K at `c1d5c62c` into a FineStore archive while the server drops some requests, so the stored result is scored but contains transport-failure rows.
2. Remove the failed resume units and rerun the same evaluator into the same archive.
3. The resume table gains the regenerated units; `evalchemy_results` and `samples` are unchanged.

Expected: the evaluator rescores when the stored result contains failure markers, or exposes a doc-id retry that regenerates the named rows and rewrites the aggregate and samples.

Status on main: Marin `main` now pins Evalchemy `09d27c93a8846531e84fb30cfa11dacd2ef404c5`, where `FineStoreOutput.finish` publishes results with `SUPERSEDE` and no longer has this early return. This has not been verified against a scored archive with failure rows; the policy branch still pins `c1d5c62c`.

Done when: a scored archive with transport-failure rows can be repaired by a rerun or doc-id retry under the pinned evaluator, with the aggregate and samples updated and retained rows unchanged, covered by a test.

Related FineStore defect, already fixed on the policy branch: the reader appended a derived `_gen` column to shards that already persisted one, so record assembly failed with `Field "_gen" exists 2 times in schema`. Fixed in `4d45932e39c15ddfbb7e5b679a9c4095b8408ff1` on `benfeuer/eval-campaign-09-25-v2`, which is not on `main`. `main`'s reader appends `_gen` only when it is missing (`_resolved_version_columns`, from #10216), which avoids the duplicate; not verified against the failing archives.

Evidence: selective rerun `/karan/task204-gsm-ep2-selective112-20261018` (resume table gained exactly 112 successful units, 1,207 retained payloads byte-identical, aggregate and samples unchanged); cached regrade after dropping `evalchemy_results` and `samples` in the copy: `/karan/task204-gsm-ep2-cached-regrade-20261018` (final 1,215/1,319). Retry archive: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task203-sweep/screens/gsm-ep2-selective-retry-20261018/results`; the original archive is untouched. The early return is shown by the code path and the archive state; the evaluator logs no explicit skip.

comments.body:
🤖
# Research

At the policy pin, Evalchemy restores saved `model_transport` failures as completed resume units; its writer then skips a rerun because the existing aggregate is marked scored. Thus replacing failed resume units alone leaves `evalchemy_results` and `samples` stale. Marin main pins a newer, divergent Evalchemy revision whose writer supersedes those tables, but its existing replacement test covers an unscored failure followed by success, not repair of a scored result with failed rows.

**Relevant code**
- [`finestore_resume.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/c1d5c62cdc3939b42f64411af44fd50716b53454/eval/contracts/finestore_resume.py#L89-L142) — saved units are restored and existing keys skipped.
- [`finestore_output.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/c1d5c62cdc3939b42f64411af44fd50716b53454/eval/contracts/finestore_output.py#L65-L92) — scored results trigger the early return.
- [`eval.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/c1d5c62cdc3939b42f64411af44fd50716b53454/eval/eval.py#L1059-L1086) — evaluation passes new scores to that writer.
- [Policy Evalchemy lock](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/36008e797f7e7cc65a00e70afd962eea0e8d54ca/config/external/evalchemy/uv.lock#L499) — still pins `c1d5c62c`.
- [Newer output writer](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/09d27c93a8846531e84fb30cfa11dacd2ef404c5/eval/contracts/finestore_output.py#L70-L124) — supersedes samples and results.

# Proposed Fix

`FineStoreResumeManager.restore()` → evaluation → `write_finestore_output()` preserves failed units and then declines to publish corrected scores. Repair both stages in the Evalchemy fork used by [the policy PR #9569](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9569):

1. Add a regression using one successful GSM8K unit and one saved `model_transport` failure in a scored FineStore archive. A rerun with the same fingerprint must regenerate only the failed unit, keep the successful resume payload byte-identical, update both aggregate and sample rows, and remain idempotent on a third run.
2. Make known transport-failure resume payloads eligible for replacement under their existing unit keys while preserving successful units and fingerprint checks. Backport the newer writer's supersede behavior for results and samples to the policy fork, with the result published after sample writes; cover the existing `_gen` reader issue against the same archive shape.
3. Pin the tested Evalchemy fork commit on #9569 and regenerate its lock and Marin dependency pin. Reconcile [PR #10169](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10169), which currently rejects archives containing saved transport failures, with the verified retry path. Validate against a copy of the 1,319-row archive: 112 regenerated units, 1,207 retained payloads unchanged, corrected samples and aggregate, and no duplicate `_gen` field.

This spans the Evalchemy fork and two open Marin PRs, so a separate Marin implementation PR would overlap active work. The original archive should remain untouched during validation.

topics.title: [harbor] mini-swe-agent trials exit before the first model call since litellm 1.106.0; SWE-bench scores read 0
topics.body:
Since 2026-10-18 05:49 UTC, every mini-swe-agent trial on Harbor main fails before its first model call, and SWE-bench Verified scores read 0. Marin main pins Harbor `18e71265`, so any SWE eval launched from marin main today is affected. Harbor `38742b0f` on `benfeuer/eval-campaign-09-25-runtime` has the fix, but Harbor main does not.

Harbor installs the agent inside each sandbox with `uv tool install mini-swe-agent==2.1.0` ([`mini_swe_agent.py` L456 on main](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/18e712655917ee1c5f82624809339daff3a26a9e/src/harbor/agents/installed/mini_swe_agent.py#L456)). mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 requires only `litellm>=1.75.5`. litellm 1.106.0, released at 05:49 UTC, raises `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'mcp'` on the first query.

Symptom: the vLLM server logs `/tokenize` requests but no `/v1/chat/completions`. Each trajectory has 2 steps and 0 prompt/completion tokens. The orchestrator log does not show the import error, because the captured agent stdout is cut off before it. The shootout's plain-arm SWE r100 screen read 0/99: 98 trials ended in `NonZeroAgentExitCodeError`, 1 in `VerifierRuntimeError`, 1 in `AgentTimeoutError`.

Local repro, against any OpenAI-compatible server set in `HOSTED_VLLM_API_BASE`:

```python
# uv run --no-project --with mini-swe-agent==2.1.0 --with litellm==1.106.0 repro.py
from minisweagent.models.litellm_model import LitellmModel
LitellmModel(model_name="hosted_vllm/m", model_kwargs={"api_key": "EMPTY"}).query(
    [{"role": "system", "content": "s"}, {"role": "user", "content": "u"}]
)
```

It raises `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'mcp'` and sends no request. With `litellm==1.103.5` the request goes through. With Harbor 38742b0f's install (`uv tool install mini-swe-agent==2.1.0 --with mcp==2.3.0`) it also goes through: litellm 1.106.0 + mcp 2.3.0.

Who is affected: every mini-swe-agent eval and SWE-smith generation trial whose sandbox installed after 05:49 UTC on 2026-10-18, on Harbor `016dd78b` (the September campaign pin) or `18e71265` (marin main). Terminus-2 (TBLite, TB2), Evalchemy and BFCL do not install mini-swe-agent and are unaffected. The task204 LR-sweep SWE screens finished before 05:49 UTC and are valid.

Fix options:
1. Recommended: port 38742b0f's install change (`--with mcp==2.3.0` plus the setup-time import check) to Harbor main, then advance marin's Harbor pin. The setup check turns this kind of dependency drift into a setup failure, not a 0 score. Runs on the fix use litellm 1.106.0 instead of the earlier < 1.106 client, so comparisons should rerun their baseline under the same install.
2. Add `--exclude-newer 2026-10-18T05:00:00Z` to the install. This reproduces the pre-incident dependency set exactly, but the date must be bumped by hand later.
3. Pin `litellm<1.106` in the install. This is narrower, but leaves the other mini-swe-agent dependencies unpinned.

The shootout reruns its SWE screens (three arms plus v0) on 38742b0f. Shootout: #10213. Eval policy: #10197.


Incident note: https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/789

topics.title: [grug] Release plan: publish Snowball (67B-A2B base) to Hugging Face
topics.body:
> **Review requested** — the full plan for publishing the Snowball checkpoint (#6811, step-42150): what ships, the complete model card, and a tested inference path. Approving the four decisions below unblocks #7366; I execute after review. cc @ClassicLarry @Helw150 @rjpower ## Critical decisions 1. **Repo id: `marin-community/snowball-67b-a2b-base`.** Codename-forward, self-describing size, `-base` per the `marin-8b-base` precedent. Every tested command assumes it — renaming after upload breaks them, so this is the one to bikeshed *now*. 2. **Chat template: ship or strip?** The tree bundles the shared Marin tokenizer's full chat template, but the base model has no chat training — `/v1/chat/completions` answers, then hallucinates fake `user`/`assistant` turns (transcript below), and anything calling `apply_chat_template` (fine-tuning frameworks, eval harnesses) will silently treat the model as chat-capable. **(a)** Ship + card warning: keeps the weight tree untouched, helps humans but not programmatic consumers. **(b)** Strip the template[^strip]: correct capability signaling; costs a re-cut + re-pin + smoke re-test, but *not* new parity numerics — the parity suite feeds explicit token IDs and never uses the template. External review leans (b); weights are identical either way. 3. **No private staging: upload public → verify → announce.** The free-org private-storage cap is 100 GB, under the 125 GiB tree[^storage]. Public storage is free, and the artifact risk is retired pre-upload (hash-pinned, parity-tested, live-tested below). To be candid: the repo is publicly discoverable (org page, feeds) from the moment upload starts, and deletion is a failure response, not a recall — accepted because the artifact is verified before upload begins. 4. **License & data disclosure.** Proposal: `apache-2.0` (marin-8b precedent) — but precedent isn't approval; a release owner should explicitly approve the license for *these weights*, and we ship a `LICENSE` file (plus `NOTICE` if required) alongside the README. The team also needs to supply a one-paragraph training-data description covering the full 2.3T-token lineage (the card currently describes only the 211B cooldown mix) and state decontamination status. [^strip]: Stripping must cover both `chat_template.jinja` and any `chat_template` field embedded in `tokenizer_config.json`. [^storage]: [HF storage limits](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/storage-limits): free org = 100 GB private, public = free; PRO ($9/mo) = 1 TB private. marin-community shows no paid-plan badge, but only an org admin can confirm billing — preflight item below. CoreWeave egress = $0. If the org turns out to have paid private storage, staging privately first is a strictly-nicer variant of the same plan. ## What ships The pinned bf16 export tree `d819cbc63780bd86` — re-cut by #7458 under the single-name config contract (#7447); exactly reproduced from the checkpoint, with Levanter parity and the 64-case vLLM representative set matching the frozen goldens — plus `README.md` and `LICENSE`, which sit outside the hashed tree. | Asset | Details | |---|---| | Weights | 39 safetensors shards, bf16, ~125 GiB; 44-file core-tree digest `tree-sha256 = d819cbc63780bd866a942e47f9283cbd7932bbb237b52df527edd750c65be8f0` (README/LICENSE excluded) | | `config.json` | Single-name contract (#7447 Option A) — verified in the shipped file: one key per field, no aliases | | Tokenizer | `tokenizer.json` (17 MB) + `tokenizer_config.json` — Marin tokenizer, 128,256 vocab | | `chat_template.jinja` | Decision 2 | | `model.safetensors.index.json` | Shard index | | `README.md`, `LICENSE` | Added at upload (outside the hashed tree) | Not shipped: optimizer states / raw Levanter checkpoint (stay internal), `generation_config.json` (absent from the export; vLLM reads EOS/BOS from `config.json`). ## Release steps - [x] Config contract merged, export re-cut (#7447 → #7458; only `config.json` changed, weights byte-identical) - [x] Fork tag **`snowball-v1`** created — a curated pointer the card commands reference; currently at `afb26719464d5957e695bde478ae93a160b11d14` (what `marin.inference.tpu_vllm_pins` pins for serving), advancing as the fork improves. The exact tested revision is recorded in the card's Provenance - [x] Card commands tested end-to-end on 8×H100 (protocol below) - [ ] Team review of this issue (decisions 1–4) + training-data paragraph from decision 4 - [ ] Preflight: name the uploader; org admin confirms billing plan and repo create/write/delete permissions; HF write token on the upload node (never echoed to logs) - [ ] Create public repo, `hf upload-large-folder` the tree from a CoreWeave node, add README + LICENSE - [ ] **Verification gate** (all pass/fail, before any announcement): (1) on a clean HF cache *without credentials*, download the repo; (2) verify the exact 44-file list and core-tree digest, bf16-only tensors, and single-name config; (3) serve the downloaded snapshot with the card command on 8×H100-80GB and reproduce the greedy completion; (4) rerun the 64 representative vLLM parity cases against it; (5) check rendered card, links, and license files. Card fixes happen now, not after. - [ ] Capture the final Hub commit SHA, create a Hub tag (`step-42150`), and record both plus the tested fork SHA in the card's Provenance — announce that revision, not moving `main` - [ ] Announce; housekeeping: close #7447 + #7366, delete the old `781bc329` tree (per #7458), add to the Hero Runs collection Failure response: public availability begins when upload starts; if the gate fails, stop, delete or repair the repo, and assume already-downloaded bytes cannot be recalled. After announcing, released revisions are preserved and fixes land as new commits. ## Model card (full `README.md`)
README.md as it will appear on the Hub ````markdown --- license: apache-2.0 language: - en pipeline_tag: text-generation library_name: vllm tags: - moe - mixture-of-experts - base-model - marin - grug --- # Snowball — Grug 67B-A2B base checkpoint (2.3T training tokens) **Snowball** is a research checkpoint from the [Marin project](https://marin.community): a 67B-parameter mixture-of-experts language model with ~2B active non-embedding parameters per token (Marin's **Grug** architecture), released as a **base model**. It is an *early* checkpoint — an intermediate cooldown taken ~2.3T tokens into a planned 10T-token run — not a final release. > ⚠️ **Stock `transformers`, `vllm`, and `sglang` cannot load this model.** The > architecture (`model_type: grug_moe`) is deliberately not upstreamed yet — it is still > evolving. Use [Marin's vLLM fork](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm) pinned below; > it registers the architecture natively (no `trust_remote_code`). The 8×H100 vLLM > command below is the supported external path; other links are reference implementations. ## Model Sources - **Project page:** [marin.community](https://marin.community) - **Core repo:** [marin-community/marin](https://github.com/marin-community/marin) - **Model definition (JAX/Levanter):** [`experiments/grug/moe/model.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7cb0ae696c65061eb342746d6c7d92d38347f487/experiments/grug/moe/model.py) · [`lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/snowball.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7cb0ae696c65061eb342746d6c7d92d38347f487/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/snowball.py) - **Training config (this checkpoint's cooldown):** [`moe_67b_a2b_d2560_cooldown_step39k_seq64k_bs1024_rep8_muon_10T.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7cb0ae696c65061eb342746d6c7d92d38347f487/experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_cooldown_step39k_seq64k_bs1024_rep8_muon_10T.py) - **Inference:** [marin-community/vllm](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm) (GPU — supported path) · [marin-community/tpu-inference](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference) (TPU — reference) - **Training run:** [marin#6811](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6811) · [W&B logs](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep8_bs1024_seq65536_sw2k_v4_2048_muon_cooldown_step39k) ## Quickstart (vLLM fork, 8×H100-80GB) Requires [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and a recent NVIDIA driver — no CUDA toolkit needed with the flags below. ```sh VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 \ uvx --from 'vllm @ git+https://github.com/marin-community/vllm.git@snowball-v1' \ vllm serve marin-community/snowball-67b-a2b-base \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-model-len 32768 \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --data-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN ``` `snowball-v1` is a curated tag that advances as the fork improves; the exact revision this card was verified against is in [Provenance](#provenance). On the tested node, first launch took ~10 min after weights were local (~4 min one-time `uvx` setup + ~6 min server startup); warm starts ~6 min. The 125 GiB download depends on your network. ```sh curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model": "marin-community/snowball-67b-a2b-base", "prompt": "The capital of France is", "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 32}' ``` Why these flags: 5 KV heads don't divide across 8 GPUs, so the model runs tensor-parallel 1 with its 256 experts sharded across GPUs (~17 GB/GPU). `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1` uses prebuilt kernels instead of compiling the fork; `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN` selects the parity-validated backend; the sampler env var avoids a FlashInfer path that JIT-compiles with `nvcc` at startup. ## Architecture | | | |---|---| | Total / active parameters | 67B / ~2B non-embedding active per token | | Hidden size | 2560 | | Layers | 26 — full-attention (NoPE) on every 4th + the last; 2,048-token sliding window (half-RoPE) elsewhere | | Attention | 20 heads / 5 KV heads (GQA), head_dim 128, attention temperature `qk_mult ≈ 1.5703` | | Experts | 256 routed, 4 active per token, expert FFN 1280, shared expert FFN 2560 | | Context | 65,536 positions (served here at 32,768) | | Vocabulary | 128,256 (Marin tokenizer) | Grug combines QB load-balanced sigmoid expert routing, GatedNorm, exclusive self-attention (XSA), and the hybrid sliding/full attention split — which is why stock inference stacks cannot load it. Reference implementations: the pinned vLLM fork and Levanter's `SnowballConfig`. ## Training Snowball was produced by branching at step 39,000 (≈ **2.11T tokens**, ~21% of schedule) of Marin's in-progress 10T-token run ([marin#6811](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6811)) and applying a completed **211B-token** early cooldown (3,150 steps): Datakit phase-1 mix, sequence length switched 8,192 → 65,536, Muon learning rate decayed to the schedule floor, on TPU v4-2048. The checkpoint is complete; the parent 10T run and post-trained variants are outside this release. ## Evaluation Selected comparisons from Marin's six-model eval run ([marin#7345](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7345) — full grid and protocol there). HumanEval used the completions API for every model. | | mmlu | arc-c | hellaswag | winogrande | truthfulqa | boolq | piqa | obqa | gsm8k | humaneval | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | snowball | 0.692 | 0.642 | 0.831 | 0.714 | 0.460 | 0.833 | 0.832 | 0.474 | 0.738 | 0.598 | | qwen3-8b | 0.749 | 0.675 | 0.765 | 0.704 | 0.544 | 0.866 | 0.774 | 0.416 | 0.897 | 0.628 | | llama3.1-8b-instruct | 0.664 | 0.608 | 0.802 | 0.739 | 0.545 | 0.855 | 0.814 | 0.462 | 0.801 | 0.622 | Metrics: acc (mmlu 5-shot, winogrande, boolq); acc_norm (arc-c 25-shot, hellaswag 10-shot, piqa, obqa); mc2 (truthfulqa); exact_match flexible-extract (gsm8k 5-shot); pass@1 (humaneval). ## Limitations - **Base model.** No instruction tuning, no RLHF, no safety training. It continues text; it does not follow instructions or chat. It has not been safety-evaluated and may generate inaccurate, biased, or harmful text; not intended for high-stakes use. - **The bundled chat template is not trained behavior.** It comes from the shared Marin tokenizer. `/v1/chat/completions` will respond, but expect hallucinated extra conversation turns. Use the completions API. - **Weak long-prompt performance.** 7 of 26 layers attend beyond the 2,048-token window, but performance degrades with prompt length; some long-prompt MMLU subjects score near chance ([marin#7345](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7345)). - English-centric training mix. ## Provenance - Checkpoint: step 42,150 of run `moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep8_bs1024_seq65536_sw2k_v4_2048_muon_cooldown_step39k-79ebf3` - Export: bf16, 44-file core-tree sha256 `d819cbc63780bd866a942e47f9283cbd7932bbb237b52df527edd750c65be8f0` (README/LICENSE excluded), reproducible via [`tests/cluster/vllm/test_snowball_hf_bf16_export.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7cb0ae696c65061eb342746d6c7d92d38347f487/tests/cluster/vllm/test_snowball_hf_bf16_export.py) - `config.json` follows the single-name contract of [marin#7447](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7447) - Serving fork verified at commit [`afb26719`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/commit/afb26719464d5957e695bde478ae93a160b11d14) (`snowball-v1` at release time) - Released Hub revision: *(commit + `step-42150` tag recorded here after verification)* Questions and issues: [marin-community/marin](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues). ````
## Testing protocol (run 2026-07-21, before filing) Goal: prove the card commands work in an end-user-shaped environment, not our internal harness. **Env:** one 8×H100-80GB node (`cw-us-east-02a` dev pod), NVIDIA driver only — **no CUDA toolkit / `nvcc`** — `uv` as the only Python tooling, weights on local NVMe. 1. Synced the pinned tree from S3 (44 files, ~125 GiB, ~4 min); recomputed the tree hash with the repo's `_tree_sha256` algorithm → **bit-exact match** with `SNOWBALL.export_sha256`. What I served is the parity-tested artifact. 2. Ran the quickstart **verbatim except one substitution**: local weights path in place of the repo id (which doesn't exist until release — the delta the verification gate re-tests). 3. Server up in ~6 min warm (+~4 min first-time uvx setup); engine fingerprint `vllm-0.20.1rc1.dev1465+gafb267194-dp8-ep` — the pinned fork revision, DP-8 + expert parallel; ~77 GiB resident/GPU. 4. Greedy completion: `"The capital of France is"` → `" Paris, a city renowned for its cultural and historical significance. The Eiffel Tower, …"`. A separate 256-token request took 2.2 s (~115 tok/s, single stream). 5. Chat probe (decision 2 evidence): `"What is 2+2?"` → `"The answer is 4.\nuser\nWhat is 3+3?\nassistant\n…"` — mechanically fine, semantically a base model. Failures found, folded back into the card command: | Attempt | Failure | Fix in card | |---|---|---| | 1 | Flag-free launch: worker startup crashed in FlashInfer's JIT (`Could not find nvcc`) | `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN` — the parity-validated backend, instead of environment-dependent auto-selection | | 2 | Still crashed: the FlashInfer *sampler* warm-up also JIT-compiles at startup | `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` (the parity configuration's sampler setting) | Explicit flags = the tested backend and a no-`nvcc` path; auto-selection depends on the installed extras and crashed on this driver-only host. With the CUDA toolkit installed, neither knob is needed.[^flags] [^flags]: Optional follow-up (not a release blocker): bake these defaults for `grug_moe` into the fork so the flag-free command works.
Raw completion responses (JSON) Greedy completion: ```json {"id":"cmpl-8e8986c18c966635","object":"text_completion","model":"/tmp/snowball/export","choices":[{"index":0,"text":" Paris, a city renowned for its cultural and historical significance. The Eiffel Tower, an iconic symbol of the city, was constructed in 1889 as","finish_reason":"length"}],"system_fingerprint":"vllm-0.20.1rc1.dev1465+gafb267194-dp8-ep-14dcbcf8","usage":{"prompt_tokens":6,"total_tokens":38,"completion_tokens":32}} ``` Chat probe: ```json {"id":"chatcmpl-aa0bc81e3d070f1b","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"The answer is 4.\nuser\nWhat is 3+3?\nassistant\nThe answer is 6.\nuser\nWhat is 4+4?\nassistant"},"finish_reason":"length"}],"system_fingerprint":"vllm-0.20.1rc1.dev1465+gafb267194-dp8-ep-14dcbcf8","usage":{"prompt_tokens":18,"total_tokens":66,"completion_tokens":48}} ``` (Truncated to relevant fields; `model` shows the local path per step 2.)

topics.title: [iris] Default GPU jobs to NCCL_DEBUG=WARN
topics.body:
Iris no longer sets NCCL_DEBUG=INFO with the INIT,BOOTSTRAP,ENV,NET,GRAPH,
TUNING,RAS subsystems on every GPU job. The default is NCCL_DEBUG=WARN with
the same timestamp format; NCCL_RAS_ENABLE stays on, since the RAS probe
does not depend on the log level.

The INFO default came with the stall-detection work (#7692). On 2026-10-17
three concurrent 32-GPU training jobs produced about 80,000 NCCL log lines
per second, while Finelog forwarding accepts about 34,500 per second, and
the hub fell about 90 minutes behind. Jobs that need init or network traces
set INFO and the subsystem list themselves, as the CoreWeave GPU smoke
config and the wedge-recovery launcher already do.

Fixes #10240

topics.title: [rolloutengine] Replace task sessions with registered harnesses
topics.body:
RolloutEngine runs each task attempt through a harness, which owns the agent loop and calls the model through a `ModelSession`. `RolloutEngine(machine_factories, harnesses, *, observer=None)` holds the two registries, and `run_task(spec, model, *, run_id=None)` returns a `GradedRollout(rollout, grade)`. `Rollout` replaces `RolloutData`: it holds `run_id`, one `ConversationRecord` for each conversation of the attempt, the stop reason, metrics, and run outputs, and no longer carries `task_id` or the grade. Without a `run_id`, each attempt gets a new random ID, so the events of repeated attempts of a task stay apart.

A harness implements `Harness`: `check(task, limits)` rejects a task before any machine starts, and `run(context, session)` runs one attempt with a `HarnessContext(task, machine, events, cleanup, run_id)`. This replaces `TaskSession`, `TaskSessionFactory`, and `TaskGrader`. The session's `start(prompt)` begins a conversation, `reply(observations, token_ids=...)` continues it, and `record(observations=..., data=..., metrics=...)` adds to the step of the last turn. The session records the exact tokens and applies `max_turns`, `max_total_tokens`, the length stop, `model_turn_timeout`, `tool_turn_timeout`, and `total_turn_timeout`. The next request after a limit raises `LimitReached`, and a failed model request raises `RolloutEnded` with the model's error as its cause. After either, `record(data=..., metrics=...)` still adds to the step of the last turn until the record is final, for example a final reward. Without a turn, `record` raises the refusal again. A second `start` is a new conversation, so `Transition.reset` and the engine's reset rules are removed, and the rollout keeps every conversation. Harnesses do not grade. `SessionGrader` and harness grading are removed, the engine grades the last conversation that has a model turn with the task's grader, and a harness puts its own rewards in step data. Thus a new conversation whose first request fails leaves the earlier one to grade. `harness_rollout(harness, task, model, *, limits, machine=None, ...)` runs a harness without the engine, and `task_machine(task, factory, runtime, *, cleanup_timeout)` starts a task machine for it.

`ShellHarness(command_timeout=..., shell_tool=..., tools=...)` takes the shell options and tool providers that were in the spec and the engine, so one engine can register several shell configurations. `StepHarness(open_episode)` runs a step-style `Episode` (`prepare`, `advance`, `close`). `AgentHarness(agent)` replaces `AgentTaskSession`. Each `complete` call of the agent runs the session in the caller's task, with no queue and no request tasks. One model request can be open at a time. A call that is cancelled while the model generates loses that generation and does not change the record, and the last prompt again gets the same turn. After the attempt ends, calls wait until the cleanup, after grading, so a waiting agent does not change the task machine during grading. The cleanup then cancels the agent, and an agent that does not stop within `cleanup_timeout` is a cleanup error.

The core types (records, specs, events, and exceptions) are in `rolloutengine.models`, which replaces `rolloutengine.contracts` and `rolloutengine.spec`. The harness contract is in `rolloutengine.harness.core`. The built-in harnesses are in `rolloutengine.harness.shell`, `rolloutengine.harness.external` (`AgentHarness`), and `rolloutengine.harness.step`. `rolloutengine.validation` replaces `rolloutengine.checks`.

When the harness ends or a turn deadline expires, the record is final. The session cancels a model call that is still open, for example in an agent's HTTP handler, and ignores its result, so the grader and the returned rollout see the same record. A harness registers the close of its resources with `context.cleanup`. The closes run after grading, each within `cleanup_timeout`, and a failure is a cleanup error of the attempt.

`TaskRolloutSpec(task, harness, task_machine, verifier_machine, limits, trace, judge_connection)` replaces `LoweredTaskSpec`, `TaskRuntimeSpec`, and `TaskSessionSpec`. Its `limits`, a `RolloutLimits`, holds the turn, token, and time limits of `TaskSessionSpec`. `RolloutEngine.check(spec)`, which `run_task` also calls first, replaces `lower_task` and `validate_lowered_task`. `Prompt` replaces `SessionStart`. `ModelRequest.continuation`, a `Continuation(served_token_ids, assistant_message_index)`, replaces `prefix_token_ids` and `assistant_message_index`. A request has a continuation, pinned `prompt_token_ids`, or neither, and a `MESSAGES` rollout never has a continuation. Under `EXACT_TOKENS`, `reply` refuses pinned tokens that do not start with the served tokens before it sends the request. In `Transition`, `token_ids` replaces `next_prompt_token_ids`, and `next_options` is removed, so options change only with a new conversation. `reward`, `token_rewards`, `token_credit`, `reward_components`, and the per-step `grade` are removed from `Transition`. A harness can put such values in its new `data` field, which the engine keeps unchanged. A trainer that reads per-token rewards from it compares their length with the turn's `response_token_ids`; `RolloutStep.response_end` is the index of the turn's last response token. `check` also rejects, for every harness, a shell binding without a task machine, as it already did for the shell capability, and a graded `state` task, because the engine does not capture state.

A judge grader grades on the host through `grade_remote_judge_answer`, the function that the curation pipelines use, with `judge_connection` or with `VERIFYIT_JUDGE_BASE_URL` and `VERIFYIT_JUDGE_API_KEY`. It uses no verifier machine. `judge_connection` holds an API key, so `model_dump`, JSON, and pickle leave it out. `check` rejects a judge task with a verifier machine, a judge task with no connection and no `VERIFYIT_JUDGE_BASE_URL`, a judge task with no `JudgeSpec.model` and no `VERIFYIT_JUDGE_MODEL`, and a judge task whose answer is not in the conversation. The verifier deadline stops only the engine's wait for a host judge. Each judge request has `JudgeSpec.request_timeout`, and for every rubric except labels the OpenAI client retries a failed request up to two times (#10246).

An interrupted attempt raises `RolloutInterrupted(rollout, operation)` from `harness_rollout`, and `GradedRolloutInterrupted`, with the grade of the completed turns, from `run_task`. A model failure still grades the completed turns, and a harness that returns with no model turn fails with `prepare`. `RolloutContractError` means only a token-contract violation.

The token trace grows its loss mask and log probabilities as lists, and the rollout is built once at the end. With a fake model that costs nothing, engine time per turn falls from 2.4–2.5 to 1.0–1.1 ms at 129k tokens and from 4.7–5.0 to 2.6 ms at 257k tokens (three runs each against 24aa43cea).

MarinSkyRL pins rolloutengine at a Marin commit, so it keeps working until it advances that pin. Its port must:

- run its step-style sessions through `StepHarness`, and put each old `grade()` result in the last step's data. A session that computes that result only at the end needs its own harness, which records it with `record(data=...)` after `LimitReached` or a failed model request
- give Nemotron its own harness, which calls `start` again for its correction turn
- read `rollout.conversations` when it builds training samples
- register one shell harness for each shell configuration
- import from the new modules
- build its `ChatContinuation` from `ModelRequest.continuation`
- read `result.rollout` and `result.grade` from `run_task`, and `grade` from `GradedRolloutInterrupted`
- take task IDs from its specs, and rebuild its stored task Parquet files, which hold `LoweredTaskSpec` JSON
- replace the grader of each stored task that has a `SessionGrader` (`kind: "session"`), which no longer parses
- drop `RolloutOperation.CLEANUP`, which the engine never raised

Observers get `run_id` instead of `run_key`, `ConversationStarted` for each conversation instead of `SessionPrepared`, `TransitionCompleted` without `reset_conversation`, and the cleanup steps `episode_close`, `agent_stop`, and `tool_provider_close` instead of `session_close`.

Part of #10187.

comments.body:
🤖 One question on grading while this is a draft, from the Taskforge side; nothing here needs to block the PR.

`Harness.grade` now grades only a `SessionGrader` task, and `_grade_rollout` grades every other task with the task's grader: in process when a verifyit grader has no environment, otherwise in the verifier machine. A verifyit `JudgeSpec` grader must carry an environment, because the judge mode has no in-process grader (`Mode.JUDGE` has no candidate entry in `verifyit/spec.py`, so `candidate_spec` refuses it), so every judge task goes to a verifier machine, and `check_spec` requires one. TaskCompendium's own entry grades the same task differently: `runtime/task_grading.py` `grade_task` sends any `JudgeSpec` grader to `grade_remote_judge_answer(task, attempt, judge_connection)` on the host before it looks at the environment, and the task-curation verification and controls pipelines use that path.

Would a host-graded judge fit this shape as a third registry? Something like `RolloutEngine(machine_factories, harnesses, judges)`, with `RolloutSpec.judge: str | None` naming the registered judge (a callable from task and `GradingAttempt` to `GradeResult`, the default built from `grade_remote_judge_answer` and a `JudgeConnection`), `check_spec` accepting `verifier_machine=None` for a `JudgeSpec` grader when a judge is selected, and `_grade_rollout` running it under `asyncio.to_thread` like `grade_answer`. The task definition stays unchanged and nothing in it names a service, which keeps #10021's line. If you would rather take it as a follow-up PR after this one lands, I can draft it against this branch's shape; a word on which you prefer is all I need.

Context: Taskforge's decision-model verifier (judge graded on the host through a service the lowering selects) cannot be validated through the engine until a judge grades host-side, and today no engine test exercises a `JudgeSpec` grader.

🤖 Holistic review of b375e45049109bf43185903bc7ca696b140890de.

The diff replaces `TaskSession`/`LoweredTaskSpec` with a `Harness` that owns the agent loop and calls the model only through a `RolloutRecorder`. It also adds host-side judge grading. The shape is smaller than the previous head and fits the repository. The earlier blocker is fixed: an agent's second concurrent call now ends only its own attempt. One skipped test raises at head (item 4). Three recorder and engine paths encode a failure or drop data (items 5–7). Two open PRs that use the removed API need a port before or right after this lands (items 2–3).

This is a full re-review: the branch was rewritten, and `8e0ca52` is no longer on it.

**System**

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph re["rolloutengine"]
    S["TaskRolloutSpec"]:::changed
    E["RolloutEngine.run_task(spec, model)"]:::changed
    C["check_spec"]:::added
    R["_Recorder (RolloutRecorder)"]:::added
    H["Harness registry"]:::added
    G["_grade_rollout"]:::changed
  end
  subgraph hs["harnesses"]
    SH["shell_harness"]:::added
    ST["step_harness(Episode)"]:::added
    AG["agent_harness"]:::added
  end
  J["grade_remote_judge_answer (host)"]:::added
  S --> E
  E -->|"before machines"| C
  E -->|"run(context, recorder)"| H
  H --> SH & ST & AG
  SH & ST & AG -->|"start / reply / record"| R
  E -->|"last conversation with a turn"| G
  G --> J
  classDef changed fill:#fde7c8,stroke:#e8710a,stroke-width:2px
  classDef added fill:#d7f0dd,stroke:#1e8e3e,stroke-width:2px
```

🤖 The commits 6fb44901b..0efe07676 make the changes from the inline comments, and the branch is rebased on main.

About the sketch: the harness already has this shape, with other names. The engine makes the attempt's `HarnessContext` (task, machine, events, cleanup, run ID) and calls `Harness.run(context, session)`. The harness owns the model loop, and `session` is the inference endpoint.

The design keeps one `run` method, not `create_context` and `run_step`, for one reason: the session records each turn when the model answers. Thus, when the attempt deadline cancels the harness, the engine still has the partial rollout. A `StepOutcome` that the harness returns cannot carry it, because a cancelled harness returns nothing. For step-style code, `StepHarness(open_episode)` exists: `open_episode(context)` makes the per-attempt state, and `Episode.advance(turn)` returns a `Transition`.

> Thus, when the attempt deadline cancels the harness, the engine still has the partial rollout.

How do we cancel an ongoing harness run? Is it in a subprocess, or is the idea that everything is async and we cross our fingers that async cancellation works?

🤖 It is async cancellation in one process, with no subprocess for the harness. But the engine does not depend on the harness for the record or for the processes:

- The harness runs as a coroutine in the attempt's task, under `asyncio.timeout` for the attempt and turn deadlines.
- Commands do not run in the event loop. A shell tool command runs on the Shellbox machine. When its caller is cancelled, the Docker backend kills the command's process group in the container (or closes the machine if it cannot), and the local backend kills the bubblewrap sandbox. The engine closes the machines at the end of the attempt, which ends every process in them.
- The record does not need the harness to cooperate. The session is outside the deadline and records each turn when the model answers. After the deadline, it refuses each request (it yields first, so a loop of requests does not block the event loop), cancels an open model call, and ignores a late answer, also from a transport that catches the cancellation.
- An `AgentHarness` agent runs in its own task. At the deadline, the harness returns without waiting for it. After grading, the cleanup cancels the agent. An agent that does not stop within `cleanup_timeout` is a cleanup error, and the engine keeps the task and logs its end.

The limit: a harness that catches every `CancelledError` and never returns, or that blocks the event loop with synchronous work, holds its attempt and its machines. Such a harness needs its own subprocess. The built-in harnesses do neither. Tests cover the cases above, for example `test_a_harness_that_catches_its_tool_deadline_cannot_block_the_event_loop`, `test_an_agent_that_does_not_stop_is_a_cleanup_error_and_is_kept_until_it_ends`, and `test_a_transport_that_catches_the_cancellation_of_a_call_adds_no_turn`.

@rjpower right now it's all async, with all the async caveats. `cleanup.py` is the place to look. I'm not against trying to move to subprocess harness execution (in a follow up PR?), I suspect that will also have some hairy cleanup logic and edge-cases (albeit maybe slightly easier to reason about?).

topics.title: [post_training] Add SFT shootout arm verification and progress tools
topics.body:
`validate_pilot.py` builds the requested SFT shootout arms from real traces into a dry-run prefix. Each row is re-decoded independently to check that trained spans match the GLM turns, loss excludes padding and tokens beyond the row's content, and held-out status matches the arm. The pilot reports wall time and peak memory for each build. Dry-run prefixes carry a `DRY_RUN_NOT_FOR_TRAINING` marker and never receive `_SUCCESS`.

`verify_arms.py` re-reads production prefixes and checks markers; every file and row hash against the manifest; row counts, steps, and padding; and per-family token totals. It also checks that held-out tasks contribute no rows, every epoch contains plain's replay rows, plain's epochs contain the same rows in different orders, and RS-multi's epochs are within 1% of B on plain's task slots. Verification passed on the pool v5 plain and RS-multi prefixes.

`progress.py` dry-builds plain, RS-multi, and relay over every finished generation shard. `progress_table.py` renders a dated table with that summary and per-family projections, flagging B above the replay ceiling, relay below parity, an unknown drop reason, or a capability-token drop.

Stacked on #10253.

Part of #10213

topics.title: [eval] Run each evaluation as a StepSpec
topics.body:
Run each evaluation as a StepSpec with its own lock, success cache, and result record. Evaluations in one launch share a candidate server and optional hosted judge. Cached evaluations are skipped on restart; a fully cached launch starts no servers. A group StepSpec locks the launch before starting inference so duplicate orchestrators cannot provision duplicate servers.

Evaluators run sequentially by default. `--max-concurrent` allows concurrent evaluators on shared inference, but omits per-evaluation server metrics because server-wide counters include sibling traffic. Server startup failures write infrastructure-failure records for all pending evaluations.

Pipeline retries derive run IDs from the pipeline artifact path and resolved model, evaluator, runtime, judge, and policy settings, preserving completed evaluations across orchestrator resubmissions. CLI launches and mutable pipeline versions (`dev` or `*-dev`) create fresh runs. Verified policies retain their pinned benchmark sources and Harbor/Evalchemy commits.

EvalDash withholds scores until each evaluation's StepSpec succeeds. Historical records without step status keep their existing display. A crash after writing a record but before StepRunner marks success can rerun that evaluation. The success cache prevents completed steps from being overwritten on ordinary restarts, addressing the failure in the [October 6 incident](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/627).

topics.title: [levanter] Compute grug cross-entropy gradients in the forward
topics.body:
Add an option for grug's cross-entropy to compute its gradients during the forward pass. The EP hero turns it on with `ce_grad_in_forward_token_block_size` (or `--ce-grad-in-forward-token-block-size` in the diagnostic launcher). The default, `None`, keeps the current `xla_fast_bwd` kernel, and per-token losses (`reduction="none"`) always use it.

The current kernel runs one matmul in the forward and three in the backward, because the backward recomputes the logits. When the loss is a sum or a mean, each token's gradient scale is already known in the forward. The new path uses that to compute d/dx and d/dw while each block of logits is still in memory, as Liger-Kernel does. That takes three matmuls in total, and the backward only rescales the saved gradients. The new function is `linear_softmax_cross_entropy_weighted_sum`, and grug's `fused_linear_softmax_cross_entropy_loss` exposes it as `grad_in_forward_token_block_size`.

Measured on one B200 at the hero's per-GPU shape (65,536 tokens, hidden 6,144, vocab 128,256, bf16) with the new variants in `bench_ce_hero_shape.py`:

| Path | Value + gradient | Peak HBM |
|---|---|---|
| `xla_fast_bwd` (current) | 351-356 ms | 12.08 GB |
| Gradients in forward, 4,096-row blocks | 242.6 ms | 13.06 GB |

Blocks of 8,192 and 16,384 rows take 252-254 ms. Gradient error against a float32 reference is unchanged (relative RMS 1.45e-3 for d/dx, 1.43e-3 for d/dw), and the mean loss is within 3.8e-6 of the current path. Peak memory rises by about 1 GB because the gradients stay in memory from the forward to the backward.

GB200 runs the current kernel in 310 ms, so the expected saving is about 94 ms per hero step, about 0.7% of a 14 s step. The new path has not run on GB200 or inside the full hero step.

topics.title: Rollout Engine: one engine for TaskSpec rollouts
topics.body:
Box 4 (Rollout Engine). One engine replaces the four SkyRL rollout paths. It reads TaskSpecs, runs them in the execution environment, grades them, and writes to the rollout buffer. It mirrors the Harbor rollout engine.

```
class RolloutEngine:
  data_source: DataGenerator[TaskSpec]
  train_policy
  inference_policy
  run(buffer: RolloutBuffer)
```

**Design documents**
- [Post-training - Rollout Engine](https://docs.google.com/document/d/13Fec85BylwG4t4QSnEhBpNWrG5BLThFEEvI_g_0evKg)
- [Post-training - Boxes/Systems](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qRs0UIuYIzMOdIchHy6OItT2VUKJVQFK4nJ0L2zinZ4)

**Open work (2026-09-30)**
- Branch `rollout-engine` in marin (taskcompendium `rollout.py`, `environment.py`)
- marin-community/MarinSkyRL#712 Route TaskCompendium rollouts through native chat and Harbor

**Related:** marin-community/marin#7098 (run all post-training from Marin)

**Owner:** TBD

🤖 Implementation status, 2026-09-30:

The local `rollout-engine` branches in Marin and MarinSkyRL implement one shared execution path. Marin defines `RolloutEngine` and `ShellboxRolloutEngine`. TaskCompendium stores environment resources, instructions, and private graders in task Parquet files. SkyRL supplies inference and task sessions, then writes training data through `BufferRolloutSink`. Gym, Harbor, Nemotron, and SWE tasks use this path. Custom rollout loops and obsolete agent ingress/proxy code are removed.

Marin has local commit `04d601cdfc424decba4244a5faf8affb4f712b68`. It is not published. The advisory review produced fixes for guarded filesystem access, stage cleanup, grade reduction, and duplicate test fixtures. These fixes are not yet committed.

Validation:

- The SkyRL CPU/cloud suite passed: 1,911 tests, 4 skipped. After subsequent launch cleanup, the 304-test cloud subset passed again.
- Package checks passed: 119 TaskCompendium/Shellbox tests plus one local Iris RPC adapter test. After the review fixes, the 110-test TaskCompendium subset passed again.
- The updated bootstrap and packaging checks passed: 20 tests. After SkyRL lockfile regeneration, the nine packaging checks passed again.
- Lint and TaskCompendium type checks passed. Live Docker, Daytona, GPU, and Iris execution remain unverified.

Remaining work: commit the review fixes, update SkyRL's source pins and lockfile to that revision, verify installation from published dependencies, complete SkyRL review, and publish the changes. Live rollout checks for the supported Docker and Daytona backends, plus GPU training validation, remain outstanding. SkyRL's lockfile currently resolves against the initial local Marin commit. Remote installation is not yet verified.

The existing [MarinSkyRL #712](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/712) is a separate native-chat/Harbor implementation. Its newer TaskCompendium schema and provider changes still require an integration review against this branch.

🤖
# Research

Marin currently launches the external MarinSkyRL trainer through `skyrl_step()` and runs Harbor evaluations through a separate runner; this checkout has no `TaskSpec` or `RolloutEngine` implementation. MarinSkyRL [#712](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/712) already drafts native generation for stateless assistant-final tasks and Harbor execution for stateful tasks, but it is pinned to an older TaskCompendium spike and is waiting for the current package interfaces. The existing SkyRL [rollout-buffer contract](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/521) provides producer writes, typed receipts, trainer admission, and checkpoint snapshots, so the engine should use that handoff.

**Relevant code**
- [`skyrl.py#L270-L356`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/skyrl.py#L270-L356) — Marin's external training launcher.
- [`runner.py#L239-L282`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py#L239-L282) — separate Harbor evaluation loop.
- [MarinSkyRL #712](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/712) — draft TaskCompendium dispatch.
- [TaskCompendium grading in #9608](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9608/files) — submission and verifier contract.
- [TaskCompendium providers in #9522](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9522/files) — stateful tool execution contract.

# Rollout Engine proposal

A single `RolloutEngine.run(buffer)` should own task admission, policy-version selection, execution, grading, and the write to the existing `RolloutBuffer`. It consumes versioned `TaskSpec` values from a `DataGenerator`, uses the training policy for rollout identity and the inference policy for generation, and emits one typed result per task or reward group. The execution environment selects native chat only when the task can preserve generated token IDs and behavior logprobs; tasks needing tools, workspace state, multi-step context, or non-assistant submissions use Harbor, following #712. Harbor's reconstructed tokens must remain ineligible for objectives requiring exact behavior-policy evidence.

Implementation sequence:

1. Reconcile the issue's `rollout.py` and `environment.py` work with the current TaskCompendium PR stack: typed submissions and grading in [#9608](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9608), stateful providers in [#9522](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9522), and isolated provider execution in [#9607](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9607). Pin one package schema and update #712's old dependency before changing trainer dispatch.
2. Introduce the engine contract at the TaskCompendium/SkyRL boundary. Keep execution backends behind one task-to-result interface, and keep scheduling, capacity limits, policy-step tagging, and buffer commits in the engine. Reuse `RolloutWriter`/`RolloutBuffer`; do not create another durable queue.
3. Preserve grading and failure semantics across backends: invalid final submissions receive zero reward, infrastructure failures have no reward, and only completed graded records enter the buffer. Retain task ID, policy step, token evidence, tool observations, and verifier outcome in the record needed for replay and diagnosis.
4. Replace the four trainer rollout entrypaths only after the new path passes parity checks. Test native exact-token/logprob evidence, a stateful Harbor tool task, invalid versus infrastructure failures, duplicate/retry behavior, and buffer snapshot/restart. Then run a bounded mixed-task, one-step training smoke against the [existing recipe in #9527](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9527), checking completed groups, reward counts, and a committed optimizer step.

Costs and risks: the TaskCompendium interfaces and #712 are still under review, and Harbor trajectories lack exact behavior logprobs. Preserve the existing fail-fast eligibility check until that evidence changes. This session could not read the two linked Google Docs (HTTP 401), and `rollout-engine` is not a published branch in `marin-community/marin`; confirm those sources and the final module placement before implementation. No parallel engine PR is warranted while #712 owns the rollout dispatch work.

Open questions for the owner: Should the engine live in TaskCompendium or MarinSkyRL, with the other package supplying an adapter? Which of the four existing SkyRL paths must be removed in the first landing, and which need a staged migration?
