topics.title: Preserve evaluator-owned metrics after infrastructure failures
topics.body:
Preserve Evalchemy's metrics after infrastructure failures. Marin's per-sample averaging loses benchmark-specific scoring, metric names, and breakdowns.

Accept partial results only when Evalchemy's reported scored count matches the valid archived samples. Partial-result recovery requires [Evalchemy #214](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/pull/214).
topics.head: 9a3e045d55db0a7d165dfdde20b7e82e94fe23f2

comments.body:
🤖 Holistic review of 83842b7e152d14bd409e23e0390d6edd99784a9c.

The PR removes Marin's per-sample metric rebuilding. When a task has transport failures, `run_evalchemy` now keeps Evalchemy's aggregate only if the reported `scored_count` equals the number of valid archived samples. Otherwise it raises `INFRA_FAILED`. The direction is sound and the shared-path check now covers `eval_step` (26 evalchemy/aggregate tests pass locally). The open issue is the order in which this lands relative to the Evalchemy pin.

**Should fix**
1. `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/runner.py:322` This PR alone makes every run with any transport failure end as `INFRA_FAILED`. The runs Marin used to recover now fail. The pinned Evalchemy (`EVALCHEMY.commit` c2548fe6 in `lib/marin/src/marin/external_dependencies.py:68`, `EVALCHEMY_COMMIT` c131e5ab in `eval_policy.py:20`) still uses `_scored_count`, which falls back to `generated_count`. That count includes the failed rows, so the count never matches. marin-community/evalchemy#214 is the change that subtracts the excluded rows, and it is open and unmerged. Nothing in this PR exercises a real Evalchemy output whose counts match. Land #214 first. Then bump both pins in this PR, with a policy version if that identity requires one. If the PR merges before that, the description should say that partial runs fail closed until the bump.
2. `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/runner.py:389` `EvalchemyExecutor` calls `outcome.result.task_metrics()` a second time. `run_evalchemy` already read and validated the same metrics at `runner.py:299`. The executor then copies `coverage` and `canonical_metrics` into locals that only forward them. Add `metrics` to `EvalchemyOutcome` and build `EvaluationOutcome` straight from the outcome fields. That removes a second archive scan, and the executor's metrics are then guaranteed to be the ones the consistency check approved.

**Tests to drop**
3. `test_evalchemy_executor_rejects_native_transport_failure_when_rebuilding`: duplicates `test_run_evalchemy_rejects_partial_aggregate_with_inconsistent_scored_count`. Both cover one generation sample with a transport failure, where the fixture's default `scored_count` equals the document extent. The `source_metric` / `benchmark_name` parametrization fed the deleted `_apply_recovered_canonical_metrics` projection and no longer reaches different code. The "when_rebuilding" name describes the removed behavior.
4. `test_evalchemy_executor_preserves_evaluator_partial_aggregates[WeightedTask-weighted_score-0.7]`: redundant matrix. Both cases are an opaque pass-through of the evaluator's results dict, so one case covers the behavior.

**Related PRs**
5. #10169 (same author): renames `run_evalchemy` to `_run_evalchemy_once` and repoints `EvalchemyExecutor` at it, over the same lines. The validation block this PR moves into `run_evalchemy` has to follow into `_run_evalchemy_once`, and the post-hoc `run_served_evalchemy` path must keep it. Land this PR first, then rebase #10169.
6. #10033: its hunk sits next to `_apply_recovered_canonical_metrics`, which this PR deletes, and it changes the `run_evalchemy`/`_run_evalchemy_child` signatures (`model` → `session`). It does not depend on this PR. Whichever lands second has to resolve the textual conflict.

<!-- marin-holistic-review:83842b7e152d14bd409e23e0390d6edd99784a9c -->

🤖 Removed a duplicate transport-failure test and redundant aggregate case. Evalchemy now passes validated metrics to the executor without a second archive read; the shared scored-count key and test name are consistent. Focused tests (31) and changed-file checks pass.

topics.title: [rl] Draft the Snowball curriculum design for team review
topics.body:
Draft here for the v0 part: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xwrIz-HSw_fI7HXqCtVxTi5PXiMrFOPpvd_4B8hm6LM/edit?usp=sharing 

----

Write a shareable design for fast-turnaround Snowball RL curriculum construction, covering the initial training pool and the quality/annotation pilot.

Deliver the draft in `docs/design/snowball-rl-curriculum.md` and publish its reviewable text here. Keep proposed behavior, locally implemented behavior, and executed data/model results distinct.

Done when:

- [x] Specify the v0 target, Ben-derived source recipe, explicit expansion policy, source/difficulty sampling, and handling of insufficient unique environments.
- [x] Pin the converted corpus and admitted catalog; define task identity, holdout grouping, evaluation exclusion, private verifier boundaries, and artifact provenance.
- [ ] Specify the fixed 10k pilot: source-stratified selection, decision-model quality filtering, DeepSeek Flash summaries/tags/difficulty, and Harrier summary embeddings.
- [ ] Define how source, difficulty, semantic diversity, and measured online learning feedback affect later sampling.
- [ ] Name acceptance checks and the current-stack integration gate; separate static quality opinions from executed verifier and rollout evidence.
- [ ] Record unresolved source expansion, storage access, bindings, and runtime compatibility decisions.
- [ ] Complete an independent cold-reader review and link the implementation issues.

The [existing capability catalog and embedding workflow](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/205558e1a7fc3dd705b1132691798b09dc1f254c/experiments/post_training/task_curriculum/README.md) supply reusable inputs. [Ben's v0.1 report](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10305) establishes the historical recipe and its limits; it does not establish a ready 100k pool or calibrated task difficulty.

Related efforts: [#10314](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10314), [#10315](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10315).

Draft complete; team review remains open. The local Markdown draft is reproduced below for sharing.

---

# Snowball RL curriculum: v0 pool and curation pilot

Status: design with v0.2 independently verified and published, 2026-10-19.
Audience: Marin RL and data teams.

Tracking: [v0 pool #10314](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10314),
[10k pilot #10315](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10315), and
[design review #10316](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10316).

Build two artifacts in parallel: a training pool targeting 100,000 distinct tasks
for a fast Snowball RL iteration, and a fixed 10,000-task diagnostic sample for
developing quality review, semantic annotations, and curriculum sampling. Start
v0 from Ben's Snowball source families. Use the pilot to decide how to expand and
reweight them. The approved v0.2 pool contains 100,000 independently verified
task contracts and is published in object storage. The private browser has
loaded all 100,000 records. The 10,000-task quality/annotation pilot remains a separate effort;
it is not a requested 10,000-task training subset.

Here, an environment means one task instance with its public interaction
contract and private grader contract. Canonical tasks use TaskSpec; historical
native structural imports retain their original contract. It does not mean a
distinct sandbox image or a generated rollout.

## Inputs and evidence

The [RL Data Atlas](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/fb11c931-5861-4878-8bb5-a964d652b45f/)
publication contains 4,998,910 converted task instances: 4,997,251 training
instances across 142 sources, and 1,659 evaluation instances. These are conversion
counts before curation admission or this proposal's duplicate and holdout checks.

| Input | Location |
| --- | --- |
| Converted publication | `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-semantics/publication-008e95e5/2026.10.15.1/release.json` |
| Reviewed production catalog | `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/catalog/production` |
| Native structural pool | [Historical data, revision `cb728a7`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-Data/tree/cb728a7636caad3fc6fa6b6ba85a49194d9d69a3) |
| Native tokenizer | [Snowball step14, revision `6783e97`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14/tree/6783e9743478bd25a9ce03ab3460e84d6a9814b0) |
| Ben's release evidence | [Snowball v0.1 report, #10305](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10305) |
| Historical mixture | [Pinned `mixture-v2.json`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/fed5a9383b92acacbe264c7e601e93d8437218d3/experiments/post_training/smartie/mixture-v2.json) |

Follow each publication source's `curation_root` to converted TaskSpec Parquet.
Resolve the production catalog's per-source artifacts to `final/part-*.parquet`
for admitted rows. Freeze resolved artifact identities and manifest hashes;
`production` is a mutable catalog pointer. Record whether each selected task
appears in both populations and retain the existing admission decision.
The native structural pool is separate from this publication. Its reviewed
import is not production curation admission. Preserve that distinction in
selection provenance and runtime readiness.

Ben's exact historical release has 69,487 training tasks, including 57,364
structural tasks. Its four NVIDIA components contribute 13,023 converted
instances in the larger publication. Thus the 100,000-task target requires an
explicit extension of his source selection. His release supplies no calibrated
task difficulty labels. The pinned mixture expresses intended relative weights
of 0.5 for each NVIDIA family and 1.0 for structural compliance, normalizing to
one sixth each and one third. Historical runtime `weights: {}` and
`shuffle: false` did not establish that exposure ratio: the exported training
population was 82.6% structural. The historical training export also needs
validation against the latest RolloutEngine API; the native API port tracked in
[#10190](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10190) is a dependency.

## Effort 1: v0 training pool

### Selection

1. Freeze input snapshots, current runtime revision, selection seed, and source
   allowlist. Preserve Ben's calendar, competitive coding, Reasoning Gym, STEM,
   and structural-compliance families. Enumerate every extension by source ID
   and its family in the selection configuration; exclude unlisted sources.
2. Select admitted canonical training tasks and explicitly reviewed native
   imports, retaining their separate admission status. Exclude evaluation
   sources, declared holdouts, and known benchmark overlaps. Record the matching rule and its
   coverage; a train label alone does not establish absence of contamination.
3. Group exact task contracts using the existing TaskCompendium identity
   machinery. Keep one deterministic representative and retain all source
   aliases. Distinct private grader contracts must remain distinct. Repeated
   public text can share model inference without collapsing task identity.
4. Allocate 100,000 slots without replacement. The approved v0.2 policy starts
   with equal mass across the five families, targeting 20,000 tasks each.
   Within an expanded family, allocate proportional to the square root of eligible source counts.
   Cap sources at availability and redistribute within their family first. If a
   whole family is exhausted, redistribute its remaining slots across families
   with capacity in proportion to their original weights. Record the resulting
   family shares.
5. Within each source, cover available difficulty strata. Use native difficulty
   or generator settings first; otherwise use a versioned manual source/family
   prior with `easy`, `medium`, `hard`, or `unknown` and its rationale. Allocate
   equally across nonempty strata initially, capping and redistributing within
   the same source. Preserve `unknown` as a stratum.
6. Select tasks deterministically from stable identities, shuffle exposure, and
   export TaskSpecs plus selection sidecars. Record requested and actual counts
   by family, source, and difficulty. Report any shortfall without duplicates.

These labels are sampling priors. A long prompt, expensive grader, or low judge
quality score does not by itself establish learning difficulty. V0 fixes the
pool and its initial sampling weights; it does not impose an easy-to-hard
training schedule.

### Current v0.2 materialization

Calendar has 9,115 available tasks. Redistributing its shortfall across the other
four families gives the following allocation:

| Family | Selected contracts |
| --- | ---: |
| Calendar | 9,115 |
| Competitive coding | 22,722 |
| Reasoning Gym | 22,721 |
| STEM | 22,721 |
| Structural compliance | 22,721 |
| Total | 100,000 |

The pool retains all 11,087 admitted canonical structural tasks and adds 11,634
historical native closure tasks. Thus 88,366 selected contracts come from 12
admitted canonical sources, and 11,634 from one reviewed native-import source.
The 244,938-task admitted candidate pool excludes the native input population.
The native pool contains 57,364 records, with 52 duplicate full contracts,
leaving 57,312 eligible contracts and no exact known holdout overlap. Together
the distinct candidate pools contain 302,250 contracts. Exact overlap checks do
not establish semantic decontamination.

Native selection balances eight structural families, then controls within each
family. The import retains byte-exact payloads, native runtime configuration,
and token prefixes under the pinned tokenizer. Full private contracts remain
distinct even when public prompts share cached inference. These native records
retain their historical payloads. A separate adapter now converts the 11,634 selected
native records into current token-preserving TaskSpecs and rollout specifications,
retaining their original identities and private contracts. All selected native tasks
passed reference/invalid scripted completions through the current CPU engine
(23,268 attempts); the other 88,366 task identities remain unchanged.

Published artifact: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/curricula/snowball-v0/2026.10.19.2`.
Independent verification reconciled payloads and counts, and the
[private browser, revision 2](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/e2bd5c9d-0f93-4ce9-b7af-3c78ca55e5d1/v/2/)
has loaded all 100,000 records. The derived native export passes the current trainer
dataset and scripted worker checks across all eight native families. Updated runtime
packages and trainer pins still need publication, and actual model inference has not
run. Canonical external grader dependencies also need runtime validation. Publication
and CPU checks do not establish full-pool training readiness.

### Release gate

Load the exported pool through the latest RL stack. Exercise roughly 100 distinct
tasks, covering every selected execution/grader contract, with additional cases
if 100 cannot cover them. Check reset, public observation, action handling,
termination, grader invocation, reward interpretation, and resource access.
Retain traces and failures. Quarantine unsupported contracts and regenerate the
allocation before calling the pool runnable. A successful contract smoke does
not establish model quality or training benefit.

## Effort 2: fixed 10,000-task curation pilot

Sample converted training tasks before curation admission so the pilot can
compare existing admission with the proposed filter. Apply evaluation/holdout
exclusion and exact contract grouping first. Keep runtime compatibility as a
separate diagnostic field so unsupported contracts remain visible.

For each source with eligible count \(N_s\), allocate half the sample equally
across sources and half proportional to \(\sqrt{N_s}\). Cap small sources,
redistribute, and round by largest remainder with source-ID tie breaking.
Select deterministically and record inclusion probabilities. The initial
count-only allocation covers 142 sources with 40–480 tasks each; recompute it
after eligibility checks. Freeze the resulting 10,000 input identities and do
not refill rejected tasks. Report every stage against that fixed denominator.

### Processing stages

1. **Quality decision.** Produce `keep`, `reject`, or `uncertain`, reason
   codes, and evidence. Review missing context, inconsistent references,
   answer leakage, ambiguous requirements, and agreement between task and
   verifier. Inspect bounded private grading evidence only in the authorized
   review packet. Preserve existing mechanical/resource checks and executed
   grader controls; model judgment does not replace admission.
2. **DeepSeek Flash annotation.** For kept tasks, generate a 15–40-word
   operational summary, domain/skill tags, interaction mode, and provisional
   difficulty with rationale and confidence. Describe the required knowledge
   and operation. Inputs contain public instructions and public answer/tool
   contracts; exclude solutions, private references, and verifier resources.
3. **Harrier summary embeddings.** Reuse the existing [curation embedding
   pipeline](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/205558e1a7fc3dd705b1132691798b09dc1f254c/experiments/post_training/task_curation/README.md#task-and-curriculum-embeddings),
   pinned checkpoint, retrieval instruction, pooling, normalization, and
   FineStore caches. Key annotations by full request/model revision and vectors
   by rendered text plus embedding specification. Keep task identity separate
   from public-content identity. Preserve curriculum matching as a diagnostic.
4. **Curriculum sampling.** Cluster summary vectors, then inspect source ×
   difficulty × semantic-cluster coverage. Use cluster coverage to propose v1
   quotas and reduce repeated operations within large sources. Embedding
   similarity alone is neither a rejection rule nor a difficulty measurement.

The decision-model and DeepSeek Flash service IDs, immutable revisions,
request limits, and output schemas must be pinned before inference. They remain
unverified. Measure tokens, latency, failures, and cost on a small initial batch
before processing the full pilot. Persist successful requests and bounded retry
outcomes; retain unresolved failures as explicit rows.

### Pilot evaluation

Audit examples stratified by source and `keep`/`reject`/`uncertain`, with a panel
size set before reviewing outputs. Record human disagreement and concrete error
types. Report quality outcomes, existing-admission disagreement, annotation
coverage, runtime compatibility, and cluster coverage by source. Keep excluded,
failed, and unresolved counts visible.

Run repeated attempts on a roughly 100-task Snowball panel covering source and
provisional difficulty. Use measured success rates and execution cost to check
the priors. This panel supports coarse calibration; it cannot calibrate every
source or establish training improvement. Training comparisons need the same
held-out evaluation protocol and budget.
Before execution, pin the Snowball checkpoint, tokenizer, runtime revision,
attempt count, decoding settings, token/turn/time limits, and pass definition.
Separate infrastructure failures from model failures and retain per-attempt
results against that frozen protocol.

## Artifacts and rollout

Each release retains an immutable input manifest, source/family allowlist,
eligibility and duplicate audits, quotas, selected TaskSpecs, annotation
sidecars, model/prompt revisions, and aggregate reports. Join records on source,
task identity, source locator, and contract digest; avoid lossy joins on task ID
alone. Keep private reviewer packets and credentials out of shared summaries
and team-facing reports. Large task/vector payloads stay in object storage.

| Phase | Completion evidence |
| --- | --- |
| V0 selection | Reconciled counts, exact allowlist, held-out exclusions, reproducible selection |
| V0 runtime gate | Latest-stack contract smoke and documented quarantines |
| Pilot freeze | Exactly 10,000 distinct eligible input identities, or explicit availability shortfall |
| Pilot inference | Pinned service bindings, complete stage accounting, retained request evidence |
| V1 proposal | Audited quality errors, measured difficulty diagnostics, proposed source/cluster weights |

After v0 is runnable, use online Snowball success, cost, and learning-progress
signals to adjust sampling weights. Retain exploration weight and snapshot each
sampler change. Online adaptation, a full-corpus filter, and any training launch
are subsequent experiments; this proposal does not claim their results.

Implementation: [canonical ingester and runtime support #10319](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10319), following the existing curation catalog and TaskCompendium converter pattern; [trainer companion draft](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/1032). The canonical converter reproduces all 11,634 selected native TaskSpecs byte-for-byte. Package publication, trainer lock updates, and actual inference remain release gates.

topics.title: [taskforge] Add the stage coordinator over the build DAG
topics.body:
Add `stage_coordinator`, which runs an item through triage, author, build, validate and review with the stage functions a caller passes in `StageFunctions`. Each stage returns an event with an exit, and a transition table gives the next stage. The item's state is a fold over its events (`derive_state`). `ItemBudget` bounds build revisions and validation retries, and the coordinator spends them when it records `AUTHOR_FAILED`, `BUILD_FAILED` or `DECIDED`. A build error from the program's own code, `BuildFailure` or any other exception, costs a revision. `BuildInfrastructureFailure` (the build host failed: a sandbox did not start, an image did not pull, a pod died), `ModelUnavailable` and `OSError` (a storage fault, a missing blob or memo) are failures the author cannot fix. Those fail the item in place at the build stage, and the next `run_item` builds the same program again with its revisions unspent. When the author raises `StructuredOutputError` because its structured reply stayed invalid after the repair turn, as when the output limit cut it, the coordinator records `AUTHOR_FAILED`, spends a revision from the same budget, and asks the author again with `Revision(AUTHOR_FAILURE, ...)`.

The `OPENED` event records the digests of the proposal and the budget, and the coordinator's model digest, the model part of every step key. A relaunch with any of them changed raises `ValueError`, so every build of an item runs under one model. The author returns an `AuthoredProgram`, the program with the Python source it came from. The coordinator writes the source to `rounds/<n>/authored/<k>/program.py`, beside the manifest `program.json`, with `k` the item's build failures so far. The build stage loads the program from that file with `StageFunctions.load_program`, so a sampling model author is called once per revision. Each author call gets its own directory, so a process killed after re-authoring leaves the program of the saved `AUTHORED` event in place for the relaunch. `stage30_author/loader.py` is the plain loader; the author PR replaces it with a restricted one (allowed imports, safe builtins). A program defined in Python, as `static_author` returns, has no source, and for it the build stage asks the author again. In both cases a build whose program digest differs from the `AUTHORED` event raises.

Events stay in an `ItemEventLog` (in memory here) while the item runs. When the item reaches a terminal, `run_item` saves the log through an `ItemEventStore`. `JsonEventStore` writes `items/<item_id>/events.json` after every other file of the item, and the next `run_item` with an empty log restores the log from it. An accepted or rejected item then returns without running a stage or writing a byte. When the store lacks the final log, as after a failed save retried with the same in-memory log, `run_item` saves it before returning. An abandoned item re-enters validation with its retries reset, and a failed item resumes at the stage that raised, with the step store under `<root>/store` serving the build steps already run. A process killed mid-item restarts from the last saved terminal, or from triage. The ledger PR adds a file-backed log saving each event on append.

The triage verdict and the review `Decision` types come along as the vocabulary the machine records; `Retry.cause` and `Modify.findings` are strings until validate returns. Validate and review are caller functions: the coordinator writes the validate summary to `validation.json` and passes review the JSON read back from it. `stage_coordinator` sits above the numbered stages and may import every one of them, and nothing imports it. The capability experiment runs a catalog entry through the coordinator with its example program as a sink-only build, to an accepted task.

The design is cut from draft #9993, and the base is #10081.

🤖 Description trimmed as asked: the paragraph with the line count, the test path and the import-test detail is now behaviour only, and the future-PR list is gone; the design source and base stay.

🤖 Holistic review of 60ea1545890268d253f7411248f906095c491268.

This PR adds `stage_coordinator`: an event-folded item machine, an in-memory log with a JSON terminal store, and adapters that run triage, author, build, validate and review over the #10081 build DAG. The design is coherent, and the 130 taskforge and capability tests pass locally. There are no blockers. Three structural issues remain: one storage fault still spends revisions, the author protocol cannot carry the model errors it is meant to handle, and the transition table is configurable with no caller and permits tables the adapters cannot run.

**Should fix**
1. `lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/stage_coordinator/coordinator.py:346` `except Exception` still records a storage fault as `BUILD_FAILED` when the fault raises `ValueError`. `RLEnvBuildStepStore.load` raises `ValueError("Blob … does not match its digest")` on a corrupted blob (`stage40_build/step_store.py:155`, covered by `test_a_blob_altered_on_disk_is_refused`), and a truncated memo raises a pydantic `ValidationError`. Neither is an `OSError`. Revisions leave the keys of unchanged steps unchanged, so every re-authored program hits the same bad memo, and the item ends `REJECTED(BUDGET)` permanently even though the program is fine. This is the case the earlier correctness comment raised and the body's "a storage fault … fails in place" claim, and only its `OSError` half is fixed. Replacement: have `step_store` raise an `OSError` subclass (or `BuildInfrastructureFailure`) for an unreadable or mismatched memo. Alternatively, reuse the frame analysis `_build_failure_line` already does and spend a revision only when the traceback passes through a program frame or the error is a `BuildFailure`.
2. `lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/stage30_author/author.py:55` `Author.__call__` is synchronous, while `ModelClient.complete`/`complete_structured` and `llm.structured.complete_structured` are `async`. `StructuredOutputError` and `ModelUnavailable` reach the author only from those coroutines. The coordinator calls the author synchronously inside its running loop (`coordinator.py:288`, `:311`), so a model-sampling author cannot await its client. `asyncio.run` there raises `RuntimeError`, which fails the item instead of producing `AUTHOR_FAILED`. The new `AUTHOR_FAILED`/`AUTHOR_FAILURE` path is exercised only by sync fakes that raise those errors directly (`test_pipeline_walkthrough.py:490`, `:532`). Replacement: make `Author` (and `Triage`/`Review`, for parity with `Build`/`Validate`) `async def __call__`, await it in `_author` and `_authored_program`, and make `static_author` return a coroutine function. Doing this now keeps the author PR from changing the protocol under every caller.
3. `lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/stage_coordinator/coordinator.py:157` The `transitions` field, the `table` parameter threaded through `transition`/`derive_state`, `check_transitions` and `CLOSING_EDGES` (`item_machine.py:156-184`) have no caller outside `test_a_caller_table_re_targets_an_edge_and_a_table_missing_an_exit_is_refused`. `check_transitions` also accepts tables the adapters cannot run. For example, `(TRIAGE, ACCEPT) -> BUILD` passes the check, and then `_authored_program` raises `ValueError(... not the authored None)` on every launch and relaunch, because no `AUTHORED` event set `program_digest`. Replacement: keep `DEFAULT_TRANSITIONS` as the module's single table, then delete the field, the `table` parameters, `check_transitions`, `CLOSING_EDGES` and that test. Add configurability when a second table exists, with the adapter preconditions it needs.

**Tests to drop**
4. `test_the_stage_functions_carry_the_proposal_to_an_accepted_draft_when_called_directly` (`test_pipeline_walkthrough.py:276`): guard mirroring and redundancy. `accept` returns a constant. The `run_build`→`load_draft` round trip is already covered by `stage40_build/test_run.py:183-202`. The next test (`test_run_item_records_an_event_per_stage…`) calls the same functions through `run_item`. It fails only when the fixture program changes.

5. #9849 (draft, `taskforge/10-loop`, with #9850 and #9789 stacked on it) adds an earlier `taskforge.loop.run_item` with an event log, which this PR replaces. Merge this PR first, then close #9849 and rebase or close its stack. #9993 is the reference draft and is not a merge candidate. #10092 touches only `llm/structured.py` and is independent.

🤖 All four applied in ab84f45f98.

1. `RLEnvBuildStepStore.load` raises `StoreCorruption`, an `OSError` subclass, for a memo that does not validate, a blob that does not match its digest, or a blob that does not decode as the step's output type. The coordinator's `OSError` path already fails the item in place with its revisions unspent, so a corrupt memo no longer spends the budget. A walkthrough test truncates a memo after a full build and checks that the relaunch raises `StoreCorruption`, records `TERMINAL` failed rather than `BUILD_FAILED`, and writes no failure file.
2. `Author`, `Triage` and `Review` are `async` like `Build` and `Validate`; `static_author` and `stage20_triage.verdict.accept` return coroutines, and the coordinator awaits them in `_triage`, `_author`, `_authored_program` and `_review`.

<!-- marin-deslop:60ea1545890268d253f7411248f906095c491268 -->

🤖 Holistic review of 5a8af84889b082d1455b95b516c708561236a094.

> **In short:** This PR adds `stage_coordinator`, which runs an item through triage, author, build, validate and review as an event log. This head also makes every stage function async. The four earlier findings are fixed. One blocker remains: an `OSError` from the program's own code fails the item in place, so the author never gets a revision.

### System
```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph coord["taskforge.stage_coordinator"]
    caller["StageFunctions"]:::added
    machine["item_machine: TRANSITIONS, derive_state"]:::added
    log["event_log: JsonEventStore"]:::added
    run["coordinator.run_item"]:::added
  end
  subgraph stages["taskforge stages"]
    triage["stage20_triage.accept"]:::added
    author["stage30_author: Author, AuthoredProgram"]:::changed
    review["stage60_review: Decision"]:::added
    loader["stage30_author.loader: load_program_source"]:::added
    build["stage40_build.run_build"]
    store["stage40_build: RLEnvBuildStepStore"]:::changed
  end
  caller -->|"stage functions"| run
  machine -->|"next stage from the folded events"| run
  log -->|"restore the log, save it at a terminal"| run
  run -->|"await"| triage
  run -->|"await, write authored/k/program.py"| author
  run -->|"await on validation.json"| review
  author -->|"source read back from program.py"| loader
  loader -->|"program, digest checked"| build
  build -->|"memo hit or StoreCorruption"| store
  classDef changed fill:#fde7c8,stroke:#e8710a,stroke-width:2px
  classDef added fill:#d7f0dd,stroke:#1e8e3e,stroke-width:2px
```

### Why
#10081 added the build DAG and the step store, but nothing runs an item from a proposal to an accepted or rejected task. The PR states the goal: run each stage with functions from the caller, bound the revisions and retries, and resume a failed item at the stage that raised. The design comes from draft #9993, and it replaces the earlier draft loop in #9849.

### Current state
At the merge base (d690a2a, the merge of #10081), taskforge has `stage30_author` and `stage40_build`. `Author` is a synchronous Protocol that returns an `RLEnvBuildProgram`, and `static_author` wraps a program written by hand. `run_build` runs the steps, memoizes each one in `RLEnvBuildStepStore`, and writes `draft/task.json` and `draft/provenance.json`. Only tests call it. The runner attaches the step name to a `BuildFailure`. Other exceptions, `OSError` included, pass up unchanged. `RLEnvBuildStepStore.load` raises `ValueError` for a blob that does not match its digest. The numbered packages have no triage, validate or review types.

Nothing sequences the stages, records what an item did, bounds the author's revisions, or resumes an item after a crash.

### How
**The item state is a fold over its events.** Each adapter returns an `ItemEvent` with an exit, `TRANSITIONS` gives the next stage, and `derive_state` folds the log again on each relaunch.

```python
# lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/stage_coordinator/coordinator.py
async def _advance(item: _Item, state: ItemState) -> ItemState:
    while True:
        event = await ADAPTERS[state.stage](item, state)
        state = transition(state, item.log.append(event))
        if state.terminal is not None:
            return state
```

**The coordinator spends the budget when it records the event.** `_failure_attrs` selects revise or reject, and `_decision_attrs` selects retry or abandon, so `transition` reads no budget. `AUTHOR_FAILED` (a `StructuredOutputError` after the repair turn) and `BUILD_FAILED` share `build_revisions`.

**Only a failure that the author can fix spends a revision.** The loom-oa-dev correctness thread asked for this split. After the earlier holistic review, `StoreCorruption(OSError)` adds a corrupt memo or blob to it. Item 1 shows that the `OSError` part is too wide.

```python
# lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/stage_coordinator/coordinator.py
    except (BuildInfrastructureFailure, ModelUnavailable, OSError):
        raise
    except Exception as error:
        attrs = {
            **_failure_attrs(item, state, error, _build_failure_line(error, program)),
```

**The build loads the program from the file that the author call wrote.** `_author` writes `rounds/<n>/authored/<k>/program.py`, with `k` the failures so far. `_authored_program` loads it with `StageFunctions.load_program` and compares its digest with the `AUTHORED` event. A program without source makes the build call the author again.

**The log is saved once, at a terminal.** `JsonEventStore` writes `items/<id>/events.json` last. A relaunch restores it, returns at once for an accepted or rejected item, and saves a log that a failed save lost (Codex).

**All six stage functions are async.** Triage, author and review became `async def` after the earlier holistic review.

`stage20_triage/verdict.py` and `stage60_review/decision.py` add the vocabulary. `test_imports.py` adds `TOP` for the coordinator. The README documents the table and run root. With the CI command, 129 tests pass and 1 is deselected at this head. `test_stage_coordinator.py` runs `d43.culinary.scaling` to `ACCEPTED`.

### Limitations
- **Corrupt memo:** each relaunch fails at build again (`test_pipeline_walkthrough.py:524`) until an operator deletes the memo that `StoreCorruption` names. Nothing computes the step again.
- **Plain loader:** `load_program_source` (`stage30_author/loader.py:23`) runs the author's source with full builtins and any import. The PR defers the restricted loader to the author PR.
- **Crash restarts the item:** the log stays in memory until a terminal. A killed process restarts from the last terminal or triage, and calls triage and the author again.
- **Stub validation:** validate and review are caller stubs in every test. The capability run builds a program with only a sink, and review always accepts it.
- **Sourceless author:** a program without source makes the build call the author again, so that author must be deterministic. At this time, only `static_author` returns such a program.

### Review

**Blockers**
1. `lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/stage_coordinator/coordinator.py:338` treats every `OSError` as a host fault. An authored step that opens a missing file, or raises `TimeoutError` or `ConnectionError`, has a program bug. But the item fails in place at build with `build_revisions` 0, each relaunch builds the same program and fails again, and the author never gets the traceback. A scratch test with a sink that opens `/workspace/does-not-exist.txt` gave stage `build`, terminal `failed`, 0 revisions on three relaunches. The PR body states the opposite: "A build error from the program's own code, `BuildFailure` or any other exception, costs a revision." Replacement: re-raise an `OSError` only when its traceback has no frame in the program's files (the set that `_build_failure_line` computes at `coordinator.py:398`). Or catch only a `StoreError` that `RLEnvBuildStepStore` raises for its own I/O. Add a walkthrough case where a step raises `FileNotFoundError`.

**Tests to drop**
2. `test_an_item_id_unsafe_as_a_directory_name_is_refused` (`lib/taskforge/tests/stage_coordinator/test_event_log.py:49`): guard mirroring. `JsonEventStore.path` calls `check_item_id`, and `tests/stage40_build/test_step_store.py:97` already tests it with the same inputs.
3. `test_a_source_without_a_program_in_PROGRAM_is_refused` (`lib/taskforge/tests/stage30_author/test_loader.py:26`): guard mirroring of the two `ValueError` branches of a loader that the author PR replaces. The walkthrough tests cover the load path.

**Related PRs**
4. #9849 (a draft in the #9783–#9850 stack on `taskforge/NN` branches) adds an earlier `taskforge.loop.run_item`, which this PR replaces. #9786 and #9848 add `triage/verdict.py` and `review/decision.py`, which duplicate `stage20_triage/verdict.py` and `stage60_review/decision.py` in packages that `test_imports.py` refuses. Merge this PR first, then close or rebase that stack. #9993 is the reference draft. #10092 changes only `llm/structured.py` and is independent.

**Carried from 60ea1545890268d253f7411248f906095c491268**
- 1: resolved. `StoreCorruption(OSError)` (`step_store.py:66`) covers a bad memo or blob, and a walkthrough test checks it. The `OSError` catch is now too wide (item 1).
- 2: resolved. `Author`, `Triage` and `Review` are async, and the adapters await them.
- 3: resolved. `TRANSITIONS` is the only table. The `table` parameters, `check_transitions` and `CLOSING_EDGES` are deleted.
- 4: resolved. The direct-call test is deleted.
- 5: changed. #9849 and its stack are still open, and the author leaves them to their owner. Item 4 now also names #9786 and #9848.

<!-- marin-holistic-review:5a8af84889b082d1455b95b516c708561236a094 -->

🤖 Fixed in 102dd4651f. An `OSError` passes through as a host fault only when no traceback in its chain runs through one of the program's frames (`_raised_in_program`, on the file set `_build_failure_line` already computes); one raised by the program's code is recorded as `BUILD_FAILED` with the program line first and spends a revision. The walkthrough gains `test_an_os_error_raised_by_a_step_is_the_programs_failure`: a step opening `/workspace/does-not-exist.txt` ends `REJECTED` on budget with "FileNotFoundError: ... at numbers, program line N" as the failure line in the file, the revision and the event. The two guard-mirroring tests are dropped. Closing or rebasing #9783 to #9850 is the author's call after this merges.

🤖 On the package layout in the review: Mark's answer is to name the packages by how the task gets built rather than by generation approach. The build package is now `stage40_build_with_program` (1ff13161d5), and `stage40_build_with_agent` follows for the agentic author in the next stack PRs. The agentic generation you describe, with no build program at all, is a different surface from our agentic author; it gets its own package when it exists.

Changelog

Sourced from buffa's changelog.

[0.9.0] - 2026-07-17

This release adds explicit limits on what encoding and decoding may produce and allocate, makes decoding substantially faster, and fixes a range of reflection, JSON, and codegen bugs. There are breaking changes in both the API surface and in code generation — when upgrading, regenerate all code with a version-matched buffa-codegen.

Encode and decode controls

Encoding now enforces the protobuf specification's own 2 GiB ceiling on every entry point, where it previously wrapped silently past 4 GiB and produced a corrupt message. On top of that default, try_encode_bounded takes a budget of your choosing and answers "will this message fit my frame" before writing a byte, in a single size pass rather than two. Together these are the encode twin of DecodeOptions::with_max_message_size, which has always bounded the size of a message coming off the wire.

For decoding, a further memory-amplification attack was reported — #301, a variant of the CVE-2026-55407 advisory but on expected fields rather than unknown ones. It is now mitigated through DecodeOptions::with_element_memory_limit, defaulting to 32 MiB. This will break your existing workloads if you expect and accept large numbers of absent messages within repeated fields. If a child message's struct is ~200 bytes, an absent instance of it inside a repeated field costs 2 bytes on the wire and expands to that ~200-byte allocation on decode — a 100x amplification. Millions of those 2-byte entries fit inside a perfectly reasonable 4 MiB encoded message: 4 MiB of them is 2,097,152 elements and roughly 400 MiB of allocation. with_element_memory_limit bounds the memory such fields may consume, charging each element's own footprint so that a 20-byte struct and a 200-byte struct are each handled on their merits. It complements with_unknown_field_limit rather than subsuming it — the two limits are applied separately, and map entries and view decoding are charged the same way. Adjust either default if it does not meet your needs.

Performance improvements

Multiple changes in this release improve decode performance:

  • Singular message fields are now stored inline in message structs by default (previously, they were boxed).
  • Packed fixed-width payloads decode in one bulk call.
  • Plain-varint payloads hoist the per-element buffer dispatch out of the loop.
  • Cross-crate inlining of generated view field decoding is restored (an unintentional regression).

Together the packed-decode changes cut decode latency by 36% on a 1024-element columnar batch and 16% on shorter packed arrays, primarily through fewer allocation calls and better inlining; restoring view inlining is worth up to 32% on view decoding. Results depend heavily on code layout. Our benchmarks build with lto = true, codegen-units = 1, and -Cllvm-args=-align-all-nofallthru-blocks=6 -Cllvm-args=-align-loops=64 in an attempt to get consistent results, and even then there is a reproducibility floor of roughly ±5%. We have watched a hot loop move ~20% with byte-identical machine code, purely from where it landed relative to a cache line — so keep that in mind for your own benchmarking and production builds.

Breaking changes at a glance

Each of these has fuller migration notes in the section below.

  • WirePayload is now opaque — a struct with private fields and WirePayload::borrowed(..) / ::owned(..) constructors, in place of the 0.8.0 Borrowed(&[u8]) / Owned(Bytes) enum. The reason is that a variant holding exactly the field's bytes cannot see the wire buffer around them, which is what the slack-aware UTF-8 validator needs to take its fast path; the opaque payload carries that tail, so to_str now reaches the validator on the custom-ProtoString decode path — the one string site the 0.8.0 UTF-8 work missed. Code that only calls the accessors is unaffected. Constructing a payload lowercases to ::borrowed(..) / ::owned(..), and matching on the variants moves to the accessors, with is_owned() covering the take-the-Bytes-only-when-free pattern.
  • Singular message fields are inline — codegen emits MessageField<T, ::buffa::Inline<T>>, laid out as Option<T>, so a singular submessage no longer costs a heap allocation per field. Recursive fields are detected and stay boxed automatically. Reading and writing fields through the MessageField API is unchanged, so most code that touches the structs needs no edit at all; what breaks is an explicit MessageField<Foo> type annotation, which still names the boxed form and will now mismatch the field's declared type. Drop the annotation and let the representation infer. Note the tradeoff this makes: an unset inline field costs size_of::<T>() where a boxed one cost a pointer, so for a large submessage that is usually absent, box_type_in(PointerRepr::Box, &[".pkg.Msg.field"]) restores the old behaviour per field.
  • OwnedView::to_owned_message is now infallible. It became fallible in 0.8.0 as a deliberate part of the CVE-2026-55407 fix, which put view-to-owned conversion under the decode-time limit; 0.8.1's accounting fix then made that error unreachable for any wire-decoded view, so the Result is now dead weight. Delete the ? / .unwrap() at call sites whose receiver is an OwnedView or a generated FooOwnedView. Plain view types (FooView::to_owned_message) stay fallible, because hand-written impls and push_raw-built views can still legitimately fail.
  • Encoders take &mut impl EncodeSink instead of &mut impl BufMut, so that a sink can flush segments without copying them. Callers passing Vec<u8>, BytesMut, or any other BufMut are source-compatible through the blanket impl and need no change; a hand-written Message / ViewEncode impl updates its signature, and one that reached for BufMut methods beyond the encoders' own subset (put_u8, put_slice, the little-endian fixed-width writers) must assemble into a concrete buffer first.
  • The size helpers take u64 — types::put_len_delimited_header, and map_codec::field_len / message_field_len. This is what makes the 2 GiB ceiling enforceable: sizes have to accumulate in a type that cannot wrap before anything can check them against a limit. Bare integer literals still infer, and a u32 variable widens with u64::from(..), so hand-written call sites are usually a small edit or none. Checked-in generated code will not compile until it is regenerated — code from earlier buffa-codegen passes a u32 into put_len_delimited_header and accumulates field_len into a u32. An external ExtensionCodec impl also swaps its required method to the fallible try_encode / try_encode_one.

MSRV remains 1.75.

Breaking changes

  • WirePayload is now an opaque struct. The 0.8.0 public-variant enum (Borrowed(&[u8]) / Owned(Bytes)) is replaced by a struct with private fields, the same accessors (as_slice, to_str, into_bytes, plus new len / is_empty / is_owned), and WirePayload::borrowed(&[u8]) / WirePayload::owned(Bytes) constructors. ProtoString / ProtoBytes from_wire implementations that use the accessors are unaffected; code that constructed WirePayload::Borrowed(..) / ::Owned(..) migrates by lowercasing to ::borrowed(..) / ::owned(..); code that matched on the variants moves to the accessors — is_owned() covers the take-the-Bytes-only-when-free pattern. The reshape lets a borrowed payload carry the surrounding wire-buffer tail, so to_str now reaches the slack-aware UTF-8 validator on the custom-ProtoString decode path (it was the one string decode site #241 didn't cover).

  • Singular message fields are now stored inline by default: codegen emits MessageField<T, ::buffa::Inline<T>> (laid out as Option<T>, no per-field heap allocation) for every non-recursive field. Recursive fields are detected and stay on Box automatically. (#248)

To restore the old behaviour for specific fields (e.g. large or rarely-set submessages), use box_type_in(PointerRepr::Box, &[".pkg.Msg.field"]); for the old global default, box_type(PointerRepr::Box). Explicit MessageField<Foo> type annotations now mean the boxed form and will mismatch the new default — drop the annotation and let P infer from the field's declared type (or, for a standalone value with no pinning context, write MessageField::<Foo, buffa::Inline<Foo>>::some(x)).

box_type_in / box_type_custom_in now normalize a missing leading dot on each path; previously a dotless path silently matched nothing.

  • OwnedView::to_owned_message and the generated FooOwnedView::to_owned_message are now infallible, returning the owned message directly instead of Result<_, DecodeError>. Every OwnedView constructor wire-decodes its view (or, for unsafe from_parts, requires wire-decode provenance as part of its strengthened safety contract), and since 0.8.1 a view produced by wire decoding always converts — so the Result only ever encoded an unreachable error path. Migration: on call sites whose receiver is an OwnedView or a generated FooOwnedView handle, delete the ? / .unwrap() / .expect(...) — or otherwise unwrap the previously-returned Result (a match or .map_err(...) needs the same treatment). Call sites on plain view types (FooView::to_owned_message via the MessageView trait) are unchanged and stay fallible, since hand-written impls and push_raw-built views can still legitimately fail. unsafe from_parts callers: the safety contract now requires that the view was produced by wire-decoding the buffer, not merely that its borrows point into it — a hand-assembled view that was legal under the old wording still compiles but now panics at to_owned_message, so audit from_parts call sites for provenance. A contract violation by a buggy hand-written MessageView impl wrapped in OwnedView likewise panics with a descriptive message instead of surfacing an error that correct code could never observe. (#268)

  • The u64 size-arithmetic discipline changes three public signatures: buffa::types::put_len_delimited_header takes len: u64 (was u32), and buffa::map_codec::field_len / message_field_len take and return u64 (MapCodec::encoded_len and FIXED_LEN likewise — that trait is sealed, so only the signatures are visible). Bare integer literals still infer; a u32 variable widens with u64::from(...). Checked-in generated code must be regenerated: code emitted by earlier buffa-codegen versions passes __cache.consume_next() (a u32) to put_len_delimited_header and adds field_len results into a u32 accumulator, so it fails to compile against this runtime. Regenerate with your build pipeline (or buffa-build) after updating. ExtensionCodec and extension::codecs::SingularCodec swap their required encode method: try_encode / try_encode_one (fallible) are now required, and the panicking encode / encode_one are provided wrappers — so a codec whose encode can fail cannot accidentally leave the fallible try_set_extension path panicking. All in-tree codecs are updated; an external codec impl (if any exist) renames its method and wraps the result in Ok. Runtime behavior also changes: the existing encode entry points now panic on messages whose encoded size exceeds the 2 GiB protobuf limit — see the Fixed entry for the full list and the try_encode* escape hatch.

  • Message::write_to/encode (and ViewEncode, the types::put_*/encode_* helpers, and generated code) now take &mut impl EncodeSink instead of &mut impl BufMut. Callers passing Vec<u8>, BytesMut, or any other BufMut are source-compatible via the blanket impl; manual Message/ViewEncode implementations must update their method signatures, and generated code must be regenerated with the matching codegen version. Note that EncodeSink deliberately exposes only the BufMut subset the encoders use (put_u8, put_slice, and the little-endian fixed-width writers) — a manual write_to that used other BufMut methods must assemble into a concrete buffer first. Generated write_to bodies now emit put_shared_bytes_field for bytes fields — copy-equivalent for Vec<u8>, segment-aware for bytes::Bytes.

topics.title: SWE-smith Harbor packages expose the fix through git history in the agent container
topics.body:
The SWE-smith Harbor task packages in `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s` (and the same layout in `mlfoundations-dev/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests`) leave the repository's full git history in the agent's container. The image built from `environment/Dockerfile` keeps a local `main` branch with the unbroken code and about 944 other branches, so the agent can print the fix with `git diff HEAD main -- <package>` or `git show main:<file>`. `/tests` and `/solution` are correctly absent from the image.

Reproduce: build `swesmith-00003`'s `environment/Dockerfile` from the package, run it with no network, then `git log --oneline` (three commits: Initial commit, Bug Patch, Remove F2P Tests), `git branch -a` (944 branches including `main`), `git diff HEAD main -- oauthlib` (the exact fix).

Impact on existing data: in `open-athena/Kimi-2.5-swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s-maxeps-32k`, 860 of 5,237 passing trials (16.4%) and 433 of 4,119 failing trials run history-reading commands (`git show main:<path>`, diffs against `main` or `HEAD~N`, checkout or restore from history, `git log -p`). Some are benign (a diff against `HEAD~1` shows only the removed tests); many copy the original file. So the reported pass rate on these packages is inflated, and trace sets built on them carry shortcut solutions: the Kimi set above, the `GLM-4.7` and AgentTrove swesmith streams, and the allkimi relay data (`laion/calibforge-relay-traces`, `kimi_swesmith` rows) that was DARE-grafted into Snowball v0 (`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign3-DARE-Linear-02-2026.10.12`). SWE-bench Verified is not affected: there the fix is not in the repository's past.

A plain squash is not enough, because `tests/test.sh` itself uses history (`git checkout <task branch>; git checkout HEAD~1`) to restore the removed fail-to-pass tests before running pytest.

Expected: during the agent phase the repository has one commit, no other branches, no remote and no reflog; the verifier restores the fail-to-pass tests from outside the agent's view (for example, ship the test files in `tests/` and copy them in, or keep a git bundle that only the verifier unpacks). For each task, the gold patch still passes, the unpatched repository still fails, and the history-reading commands above return nothing.

Done when: a fixed package build exists with that validation on a sample of tasks, existing SWE-smith pass rates and training sets built on the leaky packages are re-reported with history-reading trials removed or flagged, and the shootout pool in #10213 uses the fixed packages.

comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The reported `swesmith-00003` image retains the pre-bug `main` branch and earlier commits, so an agent can recover the fix from Git history. Removing old refs alone is insufficient if the object database still contains the clean tree; the current verifier also uses `HEAD~1` to recover fail-to-pass tests. The reported 860/5,237 passing and 433/4,119 failing history-reading trials are contamination candidates, not yet an audited count of trials that copied the fix. Marin consumes these external packages and traces, while the package builder is outside this checkout.

**Relevant code and artifacts**
- [DCAgent package release](https://huggingface.co/datasets/DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s) — affected task source.
- [Shootout #10213](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10213) — waits for stripped packages.
- [AgentTrove ingestion](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/agenttrove.py#L17) — SWE-smith trace consumer.
- [Relay source PR #10027](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10027) — registers Kimi SWE-smith rows.

# Proposal

## Outcome

Publish an immutable, revision-pinned Harbor package release whose agent image contains the bugged working tree in one new Git repository with one commit, one task branch, no `main`/remote/tags/reflog, and no recoverable old objects. Keep the fail-to-pass test payload in Harbor's verifier-only `tests/` area and copy it into the repository when scoring. Record the old and new package revisions and per-task content digests; do not overwrite the release used by existing trials.

## Plan

1. Change the package producer to create a fresh `.git` after applying each bug patch, rather than squashing the existing repository in place. Export required test files from the source package into verifier-only storage before discarding history. Make `tests/test.sh` restore those files without `git checkout` or `HEAD~1`; keep `solution/` and `tests/` out of the agent container.
2. Validate a stratified sample across repositories and test layouts in offline Harbor runs. In each agent image, require one reachable commit and no old refs, remotes, reflogs, or dangling objects containing the clean fix. Exercise `git show main:<file>`, `git diff HEAD main -- <package>`, `git show HEAD~1`, `git log -p`, and `git fsck --unreachable`; none may reveal the clean file. For each sampled task, the untouched bugged tree must score 0 and the gold patch must score 1 under the revised verifier. Publish task IDs, package digests, commands, and results with the new release.
3. Audit the Kimi, GLM-4.7, AgentTrove, and allkimi relay/Snowball v0 provenance at trial or row level. Classify history commands as benign inspection, fix recovery, or unresolved; report raw and unflagged success rates with denominators, plus counts by outcome and category. Publish flagged row IDs or a reproducible manifest and clean-filtered trace revisions where the source can be republished. Annotate existing model and dataset results; filtering rows cannot undo training already performed on Snowball v0.
4. Pin the fixed package revision in the #10213 SWE-smith pool and block the eight-attempt generation until the package validation passes. Keep the already stated pilot-trace history filter separate from the new pool validation. Coordinate Harbor release acquisition with [#10198](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10198); its cache work does not repair the package contents.

## Risks and open questions

The package producer and release permissions are external to this repository, so the new dataset revision needs an owner with access to that build pipeline. The verifier payload must be checked against every sampled task's required test files; a one-commit image can still give false rewards if a file is omitted. Excluding all history-reading trials gives a conservative subset, not an unbiased replacement for a fresh evaluation on fixed packages.

🤖 A fresh GLM 5.3 trial on the raw package used the history to check its fix.

**Setup:** `swesmith-00003` from `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s` (revision 78b0d879), unchanged. Harbor at `marin-community/harbor@016dd78b`, mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 with a 32k context, Daytona sandbox, GLM 5.3 through the internal bulk service. The trial passed (reward 1, 16 model calls).

**History use in the trajectory:**
- Step 6: `git log --oneline -5 && git status` showed `Remove F2P Tests` / `Bug Patch` / `Initial commit`.
- Step 8: `git log --all --oneline -- oauthlib/oauth2/rfc8628/endpoints/device_authorization.py && git show 614b134:oauthlib/oauth2/rfc8628/endpoints/device_authorization.py`. The second command prints the pre-bug file (`614b134` is `Initial commit`).
- Step 17: `git diff 614b134 -- oauthlib/oauth2/rfc8628/endpoints/device_authorization.py && echo "IDENTICAL TO ORIGINAL"` printed `IDENTICAL TO ORIGINAL`. The agent confirmed that its edit matches the original file before submitting.

GLM made the edit itself at step 10, after reading the original file at step 8. So this pass is history-assisted, and a GLM pass rate on these packages would be inflated in the same way as the Kimi data.

**Visibility probe:** an oracle-agent probe printed the container state during the agent phase (no model calls).
- `/testbed`: 944 branches (`main`, the task branch, `remotes/origin/*` for every task), and `git log --all` lists every task's `Bug Patch` / `Remove F2P Tests` commits.
- `/tests`: absent.
- `/solution`: absent for model agents. Harbor uploads it only for the oracle agent.
- None of the other task files are present (`task.json`, `test_*_state.py`, `setup.sh`, `container.def`, `test_state.py`).

**Run folders:** `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/generation/dryrun/swe-dry3` (trajectory: `swesmith-00003__LQ7xGdF/attempts/000/agent/trajectory.json`) and `.../dryrun/visibility1`.

**Consequence for the SFT-shootout teacher pilot (#10213):** the SWE-smith 200x2 pass-rate pilot will run only on the history-stripped packages.

🤖 Fixed SWE-smith packages for the #10213 pool, with validation on 20 tasks. The same class of leak is also present in TMax.

**Fixed packages.** `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/pool/swesmith-packages.parquet` (sha256 `f004b109edf8aa9274693c07e01266d14469ec8c61fe695cc516aa1175117407`), 2,100 tasks. The schema is the same as the DCAgent parquet (`path`, `task_binary`), and the folder names are unchanged. The source is `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s@78b0d879`. The upstream dataset is not modified. Code: [`experiments/post_training/sft_shootout_pool/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/3bc613878c/experiments/post_training/sft_shootout_pool) on branch `task/206`.

- `environment/Dockerfile`: after the upstream `git fetch && git checkout <instance>`, the same `RUN` replaces the repository: `rm -rf .git && git init && git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main && git add -A && git commit -m "Initial commit" && git reflog expire --expire=now --all && git gc --prune=now`. This is a new `.git`, not a squash, so no old objects remain in the container's filesystem. The base image's lower layers still hold the old `.git`, but the container cannot read them.
- `tests/f2p_restore/`: the files that the upstream `git checkout HEAD~1` would change, at their parent contents, plus `deleted.txt`. They are computed from a bare clone of `github.com/swesmith/<repo>`. On `swesmith-00003` they match the image's own `git show HEAD~1:<path>` byte for byte.
- `tests/test.sh`: `git checkout <instance>; git checkout HEAD~1;` is replaced by `cp -a /tests/f2p_restore/files/. /testbed/` plus the deletions. The rest is unchanged. Harbor uploads `tests/` only to the verifier (checked in harbor 0.24.0 `verifier/verifier.py`; only `agents/oracle.py` uploads `solution/`).

**Validation** on 20 pool tasks, one from each of 20 repos, in local Docker following Harbor's phase order:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Agent-phase repository: 1 commit, 1 branch, 0 remotes, empty reflog, no `HEAD~1`/`main~1`/`origin/main`/`master` | 20/20 |
| Gold patch (`solution/solve.sh`) then `tests/test.sh`: reward 1 | 20/20 |
| Unpatched tree: reward 0 | 19/20 |
| Leak commands (`git log --all -p`, `git show HEAD~1`, `git diff HEAD main`, `git diff HEAD~1`, `git fsck --unreachable --lost-found`, `git stash list -p`, `git show main:<every file>`) print a clean-only line | 0/20 (upstream `swesmith-00003` control: 2/2) |

- `swesmith-01094` (`ariga/atlas`) also scores 1 unpatched with the unmodified upstream package, so its verifier does not detect the bug. This is an upstream defect, and it means DCAgent's "oracle verified" does not imply that an unpatched run fails.
- "Clean-only line": a source line the Bug Patch removed that occurs nowhere in the bugged tree. 7 of the 20 tasks have none, so only the ref checks apply to them.
- The filesystem search found no git leak. It did find copies of clean lines in installed packages: `setuptools/_vendor/typeguard` is an older vendored typeguard, which is relevant for `agronholm/typeguard` tasks (57 in the pool). The `_pytest` (iniconfig) and `rapidfuzz` (thefuzz) hits are probably coincidental.
- Residual: `github.com/swesmith/<repo>` is public and keeps every instance branch, so an agent with internet access can still fetch the fix. In the Kimi traces this happened once (`git fetch origin; git show origin/main:<file>`).

Per-task results: `pool/swesmith-validation-20.jsonl` and `pool/swesmith-leak-probe-20.jsonl`.

**TMax: same class of leak, different mechanism.** In `allenai/TMax-SFT-16.5K@848e2182` `tasks.zip`, 221 of 2,200 environments build verifier assets into the agent's image (for example `/opt/oracle/<reference program>`, `/app/verifier/ground_truth_valid_events.txt`, `/home/user/oracle.py`), and `test_final_state.py` reads them. In 181 of the 221, the instruction never names the path. In the #202 Qwen3.6-27B success traces (`allenai/tmax-sft`), 63 trajectories across 18 tasks name one of these hidden paths in a bash command. That is a heuristic: naming a path doesn't prove the answer was copied. The pool excludes the 181 (`excluded.jsonl`, `leak_risk=hidden_verifier_assets`) and keeps the 40 visible ones. TMax's Harbor converter (`hamishivi/tmax@6d3d606c`) does not copy `task.json` (including its `truth` field), `solutions/`, `setup.sh` or `test_initial_state.py`; `test_final_state.py` goes only to `tests/`.

**Effect on #202's pilot training set:** 860 Kimi history-reading passes and those 63 TMax trajectories were removed before training (manifest `selection.swesmith_git_history_rule` and `selection.tmax_hidden_asset_rule`).

🤖 The public `github.com/swesmith` mirrors are now unreachable while the agent runs, and a second leak was found in mini-swe-agent's own install.

**TL;DR**
- During the agent phase, the sandbox can reach only the model proxy. github.com, PyPI, apt and every other host fail DNS, and direct-IP HTTPS (GitHub 140.82.112.3, 140.82.114.4; 1.1.1.1) has its TLS handshake cut. Setup and the verifier keep full network.
- mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 installs a tool env that the agent can read. It holds clean copies of three pool repos: pygments, pandas, tenacity. GLM read `tenacity/retry.py` from it and called it "the reference". The conda base in the images also holds boltons 23.0.0. All four repos (469 tasks) are excluded from pool P.

**Why not a whole-trial block:** Harbor sets the Daytona network policy once per sandbox. Both the mini-swe-agent install and the SWE-smith verifier (`tests/test.sh`) download uv from github.com releases (`astral.sh/uv/0.7.13/install.sh`), so a whole-trial allow-list without github.com breaks them.

**Mechanism** ([`harbor_agents/trial_agents.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1555295d4d5a233e1bb854c814b927c21889574c/experiments/post_training/sft_shootout/harbor_agents/trial_agents.py), `AgentPhaseNetwork`, branch `task/207` @ `1555295d`): just before the agent's run, the live sandbox is switched to `domain_allow_list=iris.oa.dev` (the proxy host). The run starts once that host resolves, and the task's own policy is restored before the verifier. Each trial writes the applied policy to `agent/agent_network.json`, and the run's `driver_config.json` records it under `agent_network`.

**Measured** (null agent on swesmith-00008, -00698, -00763; HTTPS HEAD from inside the sandbox):

| Target | Before | Agent phase | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `https://github.com/swesmith` | 200 | DNS failure | 200 |
| `api.github.com`, `raw.githubusercontent.com`, `codeload.github.com` | 200 | DNS failure | 200 |
| `https://140.82.112.3/`, `https://140.82.114.4/` (GitHub by IP) | 200 | TLS handshake cut | 200 |
| `https://1.1.1.1/` | 403 | TLS handshake cut | 403 |
| `pypi.org`, `deb.debian.org`, `archive.ubuntu.com`, `www.google.com` | 200 | DNS failure | 200 |

On these unchanged trees the verifier completed afterwards and scored 0, as expected. With GLM (`swe-net2`), 3/3 trials passed under the limit, and all 76 proxy calls returned 200. In one trial GLM ran `pip install pytest ...` and saw `No internet`.

**Tool-env leak:** in `swe-net2/swesmith-00763` (jd/tenacity), GLM ran `sed -n '136,175p' /root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/tenacity/retry.py`. A probe ran mini-swe-agent's real setup on one task from each of the 36 repos (`toolenv2`). It found the same 80 distributions on every image. Only three of them are pool repos: pygments (222 tasks), pandas (196) and tenacity (30). Every conda-based image also ships conda's own `boltons-23.0.0` under `/opt/miniconda3/pkgs`, including the mahmoud/boltons image (21 tasks). The install is now pinned (`mini-swe-agent-2.1.0-constraints.txt`, sha256 `c67d1ee2…`, Python 3.12), so this set cannot drift between the pilot and the full run. SWE-smith ingestion also drops any trace whose commands or outputs touch `/root/.local/share/uv/tools/`.

**Run folders** (`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/generation/dryrun/`):
- `netprobe2`, `netprobe3`, `netprobe4`: network probes; `agent/network_probe.json` per trial.
- `swe-net2`: GLM trials under the limit.
- `toolenv2`: tool-env listing; union in `tool_env.json`.

🤖 More of the #10212 leak class: clean copies of the code the agent must fix, readable in the sandbox without git. The SWE-smith shootout pool is now at v4.

| Where | Found by | Pool repos affected |
|---|---|---|
| mini-swe-agent's own tool env, installed in the sandbox at agent setup (`/root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/`) | #207 run swe-net2: GLM read `tenacity/retry.py` there and called it "the reference". Then #207's probe ran mini-swe-agent's real setup with the pinned dependency set on one task per repo. | pygments, pandas, tenacity |
| conda's package cache in every conda image (`/opt/miniconda3/pkgs/boltons-23.0.0-*`) | the same #207 probe | boltons |
| pip/setuptools vendored copies and an installed egg in the base images | the base-image check: a suffix pass plus a name pass over every file outside `/testbed` | chardet, tomli, inflect, dataset |

What was removed in each version:

| Version | Repo or task | Tasks removed | Reason (`leak_risk`) | Where the clean copy lives |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| v1 | 181 TMax environments | 181 | `hidden_verifier_assets` | verifier assets (oracle programs, ground-truth files) built into the image, not named in the instruction |
| v2 | `agronholm/typeguard` | 57 | `vendored_clean_copy` | `setuptools/_vendor/typeguard` |
| v2 | `swesmith-01094` (`ariga/atlas`) | 1 | `broken_verifier` | (no copy: the verifier scores the unpatched tree 1, upstream too) |
| v3 | `pygments/pygments` | 222 | `agent_tool_clean_copy` | mini-swe-agent's tool env, `/root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/` (installed at agent setup) |
| v3 | `pandas-dev/pandas` | 196 | `agent_tool_clean_copy` | same |
| v3 | `jd/tenacity` | 30 | `agent_tool_clean_copy` | same |
| v3 | `mahmoud/boltons` | 21 | `image_level_clean_copy` | `/opt/miniconda3/pkgs/boltons-23.0.0-*/` (conda depends on boltons) |
| v4 | `chardet/chardet` | 10 | `image_level_clean_copy` | `pip/_vendor/chardet` (base env, conda pkgs, `/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages`) |
| v4 | `hukkin/tomli` | 23 | `image_level_clean_copy` | `pip/_vendor/tomli`, `setuptools/_vendor/tomli` (testbed env, base env, conda pkgs) |
| v4 | `jaraco/inflect` | 27 | `image_level_clean_copy` | `setuptools/_vendor/inflect` (testbed env, conda pkgs) |
| v4 | `pudo/dataset` | 13 | `image_level_clean_copy` | `dataset-1.6.2-py3.10.egg` in the testbed env site-packages |

Defenses now in place:

- **Pool:** every repo above is removed from pool v4. The SWE-smith family is topped back up to 2,100 from the 28 remaining repos, which the base-image check found clean. The method and per-repo evidence are in `image-check-v4.jsonl` and `manifest.json` `clean_copy_probe` (`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/pool/`, mirrored at [open-athena/Snowball-SFT-Shootout-Pool-2026.10@ac4e9c3f](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-SFT-Shootout-Pool-2026.10/tree/ac4e9c3fee6612c1d8ceecb0aa22950c4bdd8a9a)).
- **Generation (#207):** mini-swe-agent installs with a pinned dependency set, so the tool env cannot drift. The agent phase runs without internet access (proxy host only), which also closes the public `github.com/swesmith` mirrors.
- **Training rows (#211):** the row builder drops any trace that touches mini-swe-agent's tool env, or that reads a library copy (site-packages, `_vendor`, conda pkgs, the Go module cache) of its task's own repo. Drops are counted per task.

Kimi and other existing SWE-smith trace sets were generated with other agent setups, so their tool environments may differ. A trace audit for these paths is still open.

🤖 Upstream task defect found while freezing the SWE-smith shootout pool (v5). These 7 packages in `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s@78b0d879` have verifiers that cannot fail. The tree with the bug still in it scores 1. All 7 are in `paramiko/paramiko`. This is the same class as `swesmith-01094` above.

| Task | Repo |
|---|---|
| swesmith-06993 | paramiko/paramiko |
| swesmith-07209 | paramiko/paramiko |
| swesmith-07315 | paramiko/paramiko |
| swesmith-07539 | paramiko/paramiko |
| swesmith-07171 | paramiko/paramiko |
| swesmith-07599 | paramiko/paramiko |
| swesmith-07659 | paramiko/paramiko |

- **How they were found:** #207 ran a pool-wide null agent (it changes nothing) on all 2,100 fixed SWE-smith packages. 2,093 scored 0 and these 7 scored 1. Records: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/generation/integrity/swe-{null,added-null}/integrity.jsonl`.
- **Not caused by the history fix:** the unmodified upstream packages were then run in local Docker in Harbor's phase order (`validate_swesmith.py`). All 7 score 1 unpatched, and the gold patch also scores 1. So the defect is in the upstream verifiers, not in the `tests/f2p_restore` change.
- **Action:** all 7 are removed from pool v5 as `broken_verifier` and replaced outcome-blind (#10213). Anyone else using this DCAgent release should drop them too: a policy gets reward 1 on them for doing nothing.

🤖 **TL;DR:** existing SWE-smith trace sets use the git-history leak. 16–18% of passing Kimi-2.5 traces read git history, and in 94% of the testable cases the output showed a line of the fix. The same holds for the 2,665 passing `kimi_swesmith` trials in `laion/calibforge-relay-traces`, which went into the allkimi relay SFT grafted into Snowball v0: 491 of them read git history.

| Set (revision) | Traces | Passes | Passes reading git history | ...that saw a fix line (testable) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `open-athena/Kimi-2.5-swesmith-...-maxeps-32k` (`1b87a9cf78`) | 9,356 | 5,237 | 860 (16.4%) | 708 / 752 (94%) |
| `laion/calibforge-relay-traces` `kimi_swesmith` (`66feab4d24`) | 4,392 | 2,665 | 491 (18.4%) | 418 / 446 (94%) |
| `DCAgent2/GLM-4.7-swesmith-...-maxeps-131k` (`e209a88db1`) | 9,437 | no verdicts | 848 of 8,241 completed (10.3%) | 723 / 790 (92%) |
| `open-thoughts/AgentTrove` swesmith rows (`b395a4307a`) | 78,246 | Kimi-2.5 stream only (same 5,237) | 5,822 of all traces (7.4%) | not testable (task ids differ) |

- **Commands:** most hits are `git diff HEAD~1 -- <file>`, `git show <hash>`, `git show main:<file>`, `git diff main` and `git log -p`.
- **"Saw a fix line":** the terminal output after the history command contains a clean-code line from the task's bug patch (15+ characters, in a non-test file) that the agent had not typed earlier.
- **Relay set's own flags:** its `leak` and `hunt` flags are False on all 4,392 rows, including these 491.
- **AgentTrove clone tasks:** 40,590 of AgentTrove's swesmith rows (the GLM-4.6, GPT 5.1 Nano and Kimi K2.0 streams, and part of GLM-4.7) use a different task format. The instruction itself says "clone the repo `swesmith/<mirror>` and run `git fetch && git checkout <instance branch>`". Every one of those sandboxes holds the mirror's full history, including the clean `main`, by design. 8.8% of them then read git history.

**Method:** the shootout's own rules, used verbatim: `GIT_HISTORY_READ` from #202's selection, and the host prefix from chukar's `repository_pytest.py`. Each task's repo and fix lines come from DCAgent's packages (`78b0d879`). Code: [`scripts/task215/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/29a6fb1919/scripts/task215); `audit.py` docstring and README list the exact regexes. Spot checks of random hits were all real history reads or real fix lines.

The shootout pool's fixed packages (one commit, no remote) and its no-internet agent phase close this path for new traces. Any SFT that used these sets' passes trained on traces that may have copied the fix.

topics.title: [taskforge] Add validation trials, failure classifier and control replay
topics.body:
Add `stage50_validate` to validate lowered tasks and replay fixed controls. `lowering.lower` lowers a draft's task for the validating host. `control_drafts.write_controls` asks the model for a round's fixed controls and checks them against the grader step's reference answer and rejection ceiling.

Before trials, `preflight` probes a grader-base task machine on the local backend once and moves it to the container backend if its setup fails there. `trials.run_trials` runs k trials of a lowered task through RolloutEngine under the messages trace. Each trial is `Graded` or `Ungraded` with one typed `Cause` from `classify.classify`, the only failure classifier; a retryable cause triggers another attempt. `evidence` totals graded trials, and `controls.replay` replays each control as a `CONTROL` trial.

The standard template's end-to-end test now lowers its built task and runs it through RolloutEngine. The infrastructure test checks the validation verifier deadline. Both assertions were held back from #10298. The taskforge suite passes 686 tests here, 95 more than #10299.

Builds on #10299; #10301 builds on it.
