topics.title: [storage] Route shared CoreWeave scratch to US-EAST-08A
topics.body:
Route temporary writes from every CoreWeave cluster to the separate `s3://marin-us-east-08a` scratch bucket. Keep permanent output roots in `marin-us-east-02a` and `marin-us-west-04a`. The d6144 hero explicitly keeps rolling checkpoint writes and resume searches in `hero-checkpoints`.

Resolve scratch storage by backend on launch hosts and workers, preserving explicit per-job overrides. CoreWeave resume searches include permanent storage, the new scratch destination, and former scratch roots in the output bucket and `hero-checkpoints`, so resubmitted runs can find their newest complete checkpoint. Explicit restore paths remain authoritative.

Remove R2 from shared job storage configuration, CoreWeave CI fixtures, and Datakit sync routing. Use the bucket registry for Datakit sync credentials, endpoint, and signing region. Keep the existing R2 bucket and lifecycle resources declared independently in the bucket stack. Finelog archive and Ducky query configuration are outside this change.

Manage the scratch bucket's nine TTL prefixes (1–7, 14, and 30 days) and seven-day multipart cleanup through `marin-buckets`. The live bucket, lifecycle configuration, and organization access policy are adopted with deletion protection. Existing jobs retain their launch environment; controller defaults take effect after deployment. After releases of `marin-rigging` and `marin-core` containing the routing, configuration, and checkpoint discovery changes, update the affected dependency locks in MarinSkyRL, Harbor, and Evalchemy.

topics.title: Enable multi-device CPU tests in Levanter and Marin
topics.body:
Enable eight emulated CPU devices in the Levanter and Marin CI lanes and the local affected-test runner. Convert the MoE, context-sharding, Snowball restore, hero optimizer, partition-inspection, and short-convolution tests from subprocess scripts to ordinary pytest functions. Preserve their inputs, mesh sizes, and numerical assertions; skip multi-device cases when too few devices are available. Keep tests of fresh-process model discovery isolated.

Fix assumptions exposed by the wider device count: fixtures select the devices required by their mesh shapes, evaluation batches accommodate the mesh, and the visualization smoke test uses one example per device at its configured sequence length. Also correct empty-mesh detection in best_effort_sharding so an absent mesh takes the automatic placement path.

The affected safe suites have 3,160 passed, 70 skipped, 5 expected failures, and 11 Tasktrove failures. All 11 failures also reproduce on main in the same local environment. The sharding and convolution tests pass with eight devices (89 passed, 3 skipped) and one device (38 passed, 54 skipped). Lint and type checks pass.

Stacked on #9119. The shared partition-inspection commits from #9118 are also included here so their tests can be converted. Follows up on https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9116#discussion_r4041152537.

topics.title: [grug] Add the quality-classifier fast track
topics.body:
* add the quality-classifier fast track: for each rung budget `B`, score the first `10·B` tokens of a fixed raw pool, keep the top whole documents until they fill `B`, and train the fast-track ladder on them
  * this PR holds only the quality track from #9371 [^1]
* `corpus_sample_cli` builds a `RawCorpusPool` from the registered DataKit sources in proportion to corpus size with `corpus-id-interval-v1`: one seeded cyclic interval in the 128-bit document-ID space for each source. it skips a row group only when its ID statistics show no overlap
  * `--label-exclusion-manifest` is required, so the pool contains no labelled duplicate group
  * one map task reads 64 normalized shards, with 128 workers. a 291-source pool has 149,717 shards. one task for each shard with 8 workers did about 100 shards a minute, and each reducer had to merge one scatter output per shard. the 10.7B-token pool now takes 25 min
* `quality_labels_cli` freezes the GLM-5.2 labels and fits a ridge head on cached Harrier features (target `(quality - 1) / 4`, 80/10/10 split by duplicate group)
* `quality_cli --stage features|score|select|train` scores the pool one time at the largest rung, then selects and trains each rung from the same `ScoredPool`
  * `--selection-method candidate|incumbent|random`. `random` ranks the same `10·B` prefix by a seeded hash and is the matched control
  * a custom scorer is a `module:factory` that returns a `DocumentQualityScorer`, with a JSON `--classifier-identity`
  * the selected documents keep the raw-pool order, so scores do not change the training order
  * the feature stage joins the complete Harrier pins (`hero_data.pinned_map("harrier")`, not the `hero_data.harrier` `StepSpec`) and converts only the selected rows of each row group [^2]
* gate the quality track on downstream capability, not on Paloma macro loss [^4]
  * `downstream_eval` scores a saved dense checkpoint on one H100: 13 OLMES-style cloze tasks (per-choice log-likelihood, acc, acc_norm, correct-answer BPB), gold-answer BPB on GSM8K, MATH-500, HumanEval, and MBPP, and Paloma/Uncheatable loss by token class, by context length, and on fixed targets at 128–3968 tokens of context. the tasks are a frozen copy (`downstream-cloze-v2`, 20,472 cloze examples)
  * `quality_judge` compares a candidate with its matched random control on English knowledge, English commonsense, code, math, and long context, with a bootstrap over runs and paired examples. better = weighted gain of English, code, math above 0 at the lower bound and no group below its harm limit (1% per English group, 2% for the others)
  * `quality_cli --save-checkpoints` keeps the final checkpoint for the scorer. the model ladder keeps Paloma macro
* loss-validity study: 99 dense runs, 14 probe selections (`probe_scorers.py` plus a local production fusion-score probe), d512/d768 with 3 seeds, d1280 with random ×3 and four selections ×2, judge frozen on d512 before d768/d1280 ([report](https://claude.ai/artifact/46KvN5W9qp7rMnMPCdcNc9))
  * Paloma macro ordered selection pairs like the capability target on 33% (d512), 41% (d768), and 20% (d1280) of pairs, 23% and 34% at d512/d768 without the longest-documents probe. Uncheatable macro: 83%, 75%, 50%. no single held-out loss passed at every rung
  * dirty web (Nemotron-CC medium tiers + HPLT) at d1280: Paloma −1.5%, c4_en −6.2%, but cloze BPB +2.5%, acc_norm −0.6 pt, code gold BPB 0.70 → 2.23
  * shortest documents at d1280: acc_norm +2.0 pt, but Paloma +10.9%, because on fixed targets its loss at 3968 tokens of context is 58% worse than random
  * quality classifiers (GLM ridge head, production fusion score) trade commonsense for knowledge: fusion within source quotas at d1280 gains 2.0% on knowledge BPB but loses 8.9% on commonsense and 9.0% on math; ridge at d1280 gains ARC-Easy +2.0 pt and loses HellaSwag −2.4 pt and LAMBADA −11.4 pt. no probe beat random
  * whitespace-heavy selection lowers the whitespace part of the Paloma loss, but not Paloma macro, so format gives no false gain when the track only filters documents
  * held-out losses have 0.2–0.3% seed SD (d512/d768), cloze BPB 1.2–1.5%. the decisions transfer: the three d1280 selections get the d512 and d768 decision
* add `fast-track-long-string-v1` for raw-corpus tokenization: split at the first whitespace at or after 10,000 characters, and reject a document above 64 MiB with its source and ID
  * bound native tokenizer batches by bytes. a local 32 MiB probe kept all 19,532,169 token IDs, and peak RSS went from 4.60 GiB to 2.85 GiB
* `launch.py` resolves the rung budget in `resolve_h100_ladder_budget` and takes a `TrainingSource`, so the quality track uses the same training wiring as `fast-track`
  * add `--seed` and `--data-seed`. `--submit` forwards `WANDB_MODE` and accepts `WANDB_MODE=disabled` without `WANDB_API_KEY`
  * the quality CLIs default to MoE and `d512`, and derive `--data-seed` from `--seed`
* run fixes
  * iris: repair missing CUDA toolchain files. put the child job and attempt in JAX coordinator names, because sibling training jobs connected to the coordinator of a different job
  * fray: pass actor concurrency to Iris RPC servers, because the 32-thread default let long waits block worker heartbeats. the inference broker sets its concurrency explicitly
  * datakit CPU drivers install the `cpu` group with `datakit`, so that they do not resolve the CUDA Torch wheel
  * artifact loading keeps absolute bucket paths, grug dispatch forwards `WANDB_MODE`, and levanter keeps eval metrics between detail intervals
* validation on `cw-us-east-02a`: one 10,695,475,362-token pool from the 291 sources other than `stack-v3`, scored one time at d768, dense models, final eval loss from the training logs [^3]

  | run | selection | Paloma macro | Uncheatable macro |
  |---|---|---:|---:|
  | d512 control, tie seed 0 / tie seed 1 / model seed 1 | random | 3.704 / 3.699 / 3.682 | 3.264 / 3.264 / 3.245 |
  | d512 ridge head | top `B` | 4.017 (+8.7%) | 3.353 (+2.9%) |
  | d512 inverted ridge head | top `B` of `-score` | 3.706 (+0.3%) | 3.513 (+7.8%) |
  | d512 longest documents | top `B` by UTF-8 bytes | 4.262 (+15.3%) | 3.871 (+18.8%) |
  | d512 shortest documents | bottom `B` by UTF-8 bytes | 3.781 (+2.3%) | 3.248 (−0.3%) |
  | d768 control | random | 3.296 | 2.791 |
  | d768 ridge head | top `B` | 3.597 (+9.1%) | 2.868 (+2.8%) |

  * changes are against the mean of the three d512 controls, or against the d768 control. a new random selection moved Paloma loss by 0.005, and a new model seed by 0.022. the d512 control is near the Hero-cache baseline (3.676)
  * each rung prefix is 10.00·B, each selection is at most one document above `B`, and the random selections have the source mix and mean ridge score of their prefix (0.6097 against 0.6095)
  * the ridge head is a domain filter: its selection has a mean score of 0.818, moves tokens from `finetranslations` and medium-quality web to PDFs, books, and synthetic QA, and improves s2orc (−7.0%) and arXiv physics (−7.6%) but not social text (Twitter +19.0%). the inverted head gives the opposite change on each of these datasets
  * the longest selection is 862 documents (mean 420k tokens, SEC filings, books, PDFs). the shortest selection is 1,223,195 documents (mean 296 tokens)
* known limits
  * `stack-v3` has documents of 79–213 MB, above the 64 MiB limit, so a pool from all 292 sources stops with an error. select the other sources with `--source` until a policy exists
  * the feature stage reads almost all Harrier data, because one Harrier row group holds about 127k rows and a pool samples each one
  * the pool excludes only the candidate's labels, not the training labels of an incumbent scorer

[^1]: #9371 keeps the Hero-mix track and the `max_train_sequences` rename. it can rebase on this PR after merge.
[^2]: the complete pins from #8270 agree with the normalized shards in shard names, row counts, and ID order. the join compares each ID and stops on a difference.
[^3]: the inverted-head and length probes in this table are in `probe_scorers.py`. W&B ran offline.
[^4]: a selection moves the training mix, and Paloma has its own fixed mix (web-heavy, long documents), so a selection can move Paloma without moving downstream capability. the GLM ridge head and the fusion score are still worse than random under the judge at every rung, so the judge is tested only on selections that do not help.

🤖 Thank you. The two concerns had different results:

- `hero_data.harrier` returns a `StepSpec`: this is correct, and it is a real bug on current main. Commit 7b3728aa2 joins the relative path from `hero_data.pinned_map("harrier")` to `hero_data.MANIFEST_PREFIX`, the same rule that the raw pool uses for normalized paths. A new test checks the resolved paths. Commit db6cb6e18 corrects the scoring test, because it replaced `hero_data.harrier` with a string path and hid the bug.

🤖 Holistic review of 1b566cc4a80a8ed63ab995cdf68777c59d286284.

> **In short:** The diff adds a quality-classifier track to fast-track: it samples a raw pool, scores it, selects the top `B` tokens, and trains a rung. It also carries seven independent fixes in iris, fray, levanter, and marin. Item 1 recommends moving those fixes to their own PRs. The track works as stated, but its pool skips decontamination and dedup (item 3).

### System
```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph dk["DataKit pins"]
    N["normalized shards (hero_data_paths.json)"]
    HR["Harrier embeddings (pinned_map)"]
  end
  subgraph ft["experiments/grug/fast_track"]
    CS["corpus_sample_cli → RawCorpusPool"]:::added
    QL["quality_labels_cli → ridge head + label_exclusion"]:::added
    QF["quality_features"]:::added
    QP["quality_pipeline: score → select → token cache"]:::added
    L["launch.py: TrainingSource"]:::changed
  end
  subgraph libs["shared libraries"]
    TK["levanter.tokenizers"]:::changed
    FR["fray / iris actor server"]:::changed
    JX["iris.jax.init"]:::changed
  end
  N -->|"ID-interval sample"| CS
  QL -->|"exclusion manifest"| CS
  CS -->|"10·B prefix"| QP
  HR --> QF --> QP
  QP -->|"QualityTrainingSource"| L
  CS --> TK
  classDef changed fill:#fde7c8,stroke:#e8710a,stroke-width:2px
  classDef added fill:#d7f0dd,stroke:#1e8e3e,stroke-width:2px
```

### Why
The fast-track ladder could only measure model changes on a frozen Hero cache. This PR adds a track that holds the model fixed and changes the document scorer, so a classifier is judged by final Paloma macro loss. It splits the quality half out of #9371, and it builds on the complete Harrier pins from #8270.

### Current state
Before the change, `launch.py` was the only entry point. It trained a dense or MoE H100 rung (d512 to d1280) on one frozen Hero v16384 flat cache through `_flat_cache_data_config`. `--match data|compute` set the budget, the seed was fixed at 0, and `--submit` re-ran the command as an Iris job with `--reserve H100`. Nothing in fast-track selected data. DataKit already pins per-source `decontam`, `exact_dups`, `verified_fuzzy_dups`, and `fusion_scores` attributes (`experiments/datakit/hero_data.py:70-75,136-141`), and the DataKit store removes the flagged documents. Iris actor servers always ran 32 method threads, whatever `ActorConfig.max_concurrency` said.

### How
**The pool is a seeded interval of the 128-bit document-ID space, per source, so source shares follow token mass without a full scan.** Row groups are skipped only when their ID statistics exclude the interval (`corpus_sample.py:187-196`). Each map task reads 64 shards.

**Each rung scores the first `10·B` raw tokens and keeps whole documents up to `B`, in raw-pool order.** `random` ranks the same prefix by a seeded hash, so it is the matched control. A selection holds at most one document above `B` (`ranked_pool.py:142-150`).

**A scorer is a worker-loaded `module:factory` with a JSON identity, and one `ScoredPool` at the largest rung serves every rung.**
```python
# experiments/grug/fast_track/quality_pipeline.py
identity = {
    "raw_pool": raw_pool.name,
    "classifier_identity": candidate.identity,
    "label_exclusion": label_exclusion.identity(),
    "token_budget": token_budget,
    ...
}
step_name = content_step_name("scored-pool", identity, version)
```

**Labels are frozen, and a ridge head is fit on cached Harrier features with an 80/10/10 split by duplicate group.** The pool build requires the label-exclusion manifest at the CLI.

The fixes that ride along: actor concurrency passthrough, JAX coordinator names, CUDA `ptxas` repair, tokenizer batch limits and a content hash, eval-metric sampling in telemetry, `raw_load` context, and the DataKit CPU group. The fast-track tests (54) and the affected iris, fray, levanter, and dispatch unit tests pass locally at head. The PR states the validation table from runs on `cw-us-east-02a`.

### Limitations
- **`stack-v3`:** its 79–213 MB documents exceed the 64 MiB limit, so a pool from all 292 sources fails. Each run must list the other sources with `--source`.
- **Validation evidence:** the probe scorers and the selection report are scratch code, and W&B ran offline, so nothing in the repository reproduces the table.
- **Domain, not quality:** the PR states that the ridge head acts as a domain filter (PDFs and books up, social text down). A Paloma gain can therefore come from domain shift.
- **Incumbent labels:** the pool excludes only the candidate's labels, not the training labels of an incumbent scorer.
- **Harrier reads:** the feature stage reads almost all Harrier data, because one row group holds about 127k rows.

### Review

**Should fix**
1. `lib/fray/src/fray/iris_backend.py:333` The diff carries seven library fixes that do not depend on the quality track: actor concurrency (fray/iris), `iris/jax/init.py:275` coordinator names, `iris/cluster/setup_scripts.py:173-188` CUDA repair, `levanter/tokenizers.py:644-681` batch limits, `levanter/tracker/telemetry.py:199-206`, `marin/execution/artifact.py:148`, and `marin/datakit/__init__.py:12`. Their owners cannot review them inside a 6k-line experiments PR, and #9371 carries byte-identical copies. Move each fix to its own PR, and keep only the fast-track code here.
2. `lib/fray/src/fray/iris_backend.py:333,742` `ActorConfig.max_concurrency` defaults to 1 (`fray/types.py:578`). Iris used to ignore it, so every actor that uses the default config goes from 32 threads to 1, which can deadlock an actor that calls itself. `LocalClient` still ignores the value, so the two backends now differ. The in-repo callers (Zephyr 100, inference broker 32) set it explicitly. Change the `ActorConfig` default to the old 32, or pass it through only when the caller sets it. Add a fray test that checks the value reaches `ActorServer`. The current test stubs the server with `lambda **_kwargs`.
3. `experiments/grug/fast_track/corpus_sample.py:349-353` The pool globs the normalized shards with no `decontam`, `exact_dups`, or `verified_fuzzy_dups` filter, while the Hero cache it is compared against applies them. A scorer can then select Paloma-overlapping documents, or many copies of one high-scoring document, at a different rate than the random control. Filter `_sample_records` with the pinned attributes from `hero_data`, and add those pins to `_spec_identity`.
4. `experiments/grug/fast_track/quality_pipeline.py:778-790` The scored-pool identity hashes the user-supplied `--classifier-identity` but not the `--scorer-factory` path. Two different factories with the same identity JSON silently share one cached `ScoredPool`. Put the factory path into `ScorerSpec` and into the identity.
5. `experiments/grug/fast_track/ranked_pool.py:49-64` `write_parquet_tables` duplicates `zephyr.writers.write_parquet_file` (`lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/writers.py:378`) through a Python `StoragePath.open("wb")` sink. The zephyr writer's own comment (`writers.py:338-346`) says this sink copies whole pages and has pushed workers over their memory limit. The token cache rows here carry `input_ids` for documents of up to 64 MiB. Use `write_parquet_file` at the five call sites.
6. `experiments/grug/fast_track/quality_pipeline.py:483-648` Rank keys are unique (source and ID), so "top `B` whole documents" is "every row with key ≤ k\*", where k\* is the key at which the cumulative tokens first reach `B`. Sort the `(key, token_count)` pairs, find k\*, and filter the raw prefix in one pass in raw order. This deletes `_summarize_scores`, `_score_range`/`_random_range`, and the second group-by.
7. `experiments/grug/fast_track/corpus_sample.py:272` The normalized ID is `xxh3_128(text)` (`marin/datakit/normalize.py:125`), so the `sha256(text)` `duplicate_group` marks the same documents as the ID, and the ID check at `corpus_sample.py:268` already excludes them. Key the exclusion and `label_split` on the normalized ID, and drop the column and the per-document SHA-256 (`label_exclusion.py:21`, `quality_labels.py:207`).
8. `lib/levanter/src/levanter/tokenizers.py:781` `tokenizer_content_hash` hashes the whole staged directory. A leftover `.tmp`, or a mirror staging that copies more files than the HF allow-patterns, changes the hash, and `require_tokenizer_content` (`contracts.py:76`) then fails the run. An HF cache snapshot with symlinks raises. Its only callers are in fast-track. Move it to `experiments/grug/fast_track/contracts.py`, and hash only the `tokenizer*.json` files.
9. `experiments/grug/fast_track/quality_labels.py:34-37` The default label inputs are in personal scratch prefixes (`marin/user/rav/...`, `marin/user/muchanem/...`). The frozen-label artifact then depends on files that their owners can delete. Copy them under `datakit/`, and pin that path.
10. `experiments/grug/fast_track/corpus_sample_cli.py:25` `--max-training-tokens` defaults to 17,478,713,344, which requests a 175B-token raw pool. That is 16× the 10.7B pool that was validated, which took 25 minutes. Also, `CorpusSampleSpec.label_exclusion` defaults to `None` (`corpus_sample.py:77`), so the exclusion is required only at the CLI. Make both explicit.

**Tests to drop**
11. `test_pinned_feature_sources_resolve_complete_harrier_paths` (`test_quality_features.py:123`): it rebuilds the path with `pinned_map` in the expectation, which copies the implementation.
12. `test_corpus_sample_low_probability_preserves_global_rank_order_and_prefix` and `test_corpus_sample_grows_integer_cutoff_until_pool_is_large_enough` (`test_corpus_sample.py:207,362`): they recompute the expectation with the private `_sampling_cutoff` and `_rank_salt`, which copies the implementation.
13. The asserts on `num_train_steps == 16669` and `training_tokens == 17478713344` in `test_quality_cli_reuses_scored_pool_for_moe_rung` (`test_quality_pipeline.py:261-262`): they project the ladder table, not quality-track behavior.
14. `test_text_scorer_selects_only_after_the_deterministic_raw_prefix`, `test_larger_training_budget_expands_the_raw_candidate_prefix`, and `test_max_scored_pool_matches_exact_rung_pools_through_raw_cache` (`test_quality_scoring.py:63,249,292`) all check prefix-then-select, and `:209` and `:389` both check the constant-score error. Replace them with two parametrized tests.

**Related PRs**
15. #9371: it has byte-identical copies of 30 of these files, including every library fix, and differs only by its Hero-mix track and older versions of four pool files. Merge this PR first, then rebase #9371 to keep only the Hero-mix files, as its footnote says. If item 1 moves the library fixes out, remove them from #9371 too.
16. #9718 (draft) conflicts in `experiments/grug/dispatch.py` in either merge order. The other overlapping PRs (#10074, #9863, #10067, #9495, #9706, #9799, #9502, #10169, #8567) merge without a conflict.

<!-- marin-holistic-review:1b566cc4a80a8ed63ab995cdf68777c59d286284 -->

🤖 Holistic review of 60653337f27d81f0eca9074c6b1c4222dd4e7a01.

This PR adds a data-quality track to fast-track. It samples a raw pool from the DataKit sources, scores it, keeps the top `B` tokens for each rung, and trains that rung. Since the earlier review at `1b566cc4`, the PR also changes how the track decides whether a selection is better. It no longer uses Paloma macro loss. It scores saved dense checkpoints on downstream tasks (`downstream_eval`) and compares candidate and control runs by capability group with a bootstrap (`quality_judge`). The track hangs together, but two of its inputs need attention before it serves as a decision gate. The pool skips the DataKit decontamination and dedup attributes, which matters more now that GSM8K, HumanEval, MBPP and MMLU decide the outcome. The judge also turns a missing or mismatched input into `inconclusive` instead of an error.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph ft["experiments/grug/fast_track"]
    CS["corpus_sample_cli → RawCorpusPool"]:::added
    QP["quality_cli: features → score → select → train"]:::added
    DE["downstream_eval (one H100, dense)"]:::added
    QJ["quality_judge: E / C / M + L guardrail"]:::added
    L["launch.py: TrainingSource"]:::changed
  end
  N["DataKit normalized shards"] -->|"ID-interval sample"| CS
  CS -->|"10·B prefix"| QP --> L
  L -->|"--save-checkpoints"| DE -->|"records + metrics.json"| QJ
  classDef changed fill:#fde7c8,stroke:#e8710a,stroke-width:2px
  classDef added fill:#d7f0dd,stroke:#1e8e3e,stroke-width:2px
```

**Before.** `launch.py` trained an H100 dense or MoE rung on one frozen Hero v16384 cache, and nothing in fast-track selected data. The Hero cache drops the documents that the pinned `decontam`, `exact_dups`, and `verified_fuzzy_dups` attributes flag (`experiments/datakit/hero_data.py:70-75,288-302`).

**Design.** For each source, the pool takes a seeded interval of the 128-bit document-ID space. Each rung ranks the first `10·B` raw tokens and keeps whole documents up to `B`, in raw order. `random` ranks the same prefix by hash and serves as the matched control. The judge reads `downstream_records.parquet` and the `text` block of `metrics.json`. It takes the correct-choice BPB for English cloze, gold-solution BPB for code and math, and the fixed-target loss at 3968 tokens of context. It draws one paired example index per task and resamples the runs. A candidate is `better` when the 95% lower bound of the E/C/M mean is above zero and no group passes its harm limit.

**Evidence and limits.** The fast-track tests and `tests/test_grug_dispatch.py` pass locally at head (63 passed). Everything else comes from the PR body: the validation table, the 85-run loss-validity study (an external artifact; W&B ran offline), and the `cw-us-east-02a` runs. No test reads a real `metrics.json` into the judge, and nothing in the repository reproduces the study.

**Findings**

- **1. Should fix:** `experiments/grug/fast_track/corpus_sample.py:350` globs the normalized shards with no `decontam`, `exact_dups`, or `verified_fuzzy_dups` filter, while the Hero baseline it is compared against applies them. The judge now scores gold BPB on GSM8K, MATH-500, HumanEval, MBPP, and MMLU. A scorer that prefers documents containing benchmark text, or many copies of one high-scoring document, therefore gets a gain that the random control receives at a lower rate. Filter `_sample_records` with the pinned attributes from `hero_data` (`decontaminated`, `exact_dups`, `VERIFIED_FUZZY_DUPS_PATH`), and add those pins to `_spec_identity` (`corpus_sample.py:444`).
- **2. Should fix:** `experiments/grug/fast_track/quality_judge.py:78-92` accepts inputs it cannot compare. A checkpoint scored with `downstream_eval --skip-text` writes `"text": {}`, so `np.mean([])` makes `L` NaN. Every comparison involving `L` is then false, and the judge prints `inconclusive` instead of failing. It also ignores the `tasks_version` and `scorer_version` that `metrics.json` records (`downstream_eval.py:379-380`; the scorer is already at `v4`). It takes `example_counts` from `control[0]` alone, so runs from different task copies are paired by position or raise an `IndexError`. In `read_run_scores`, raise when no set has `fixed_target_documents >= 5`. In `judge`, require equal versions and equal `example_id` arrays for each task across all runs.
- **3. topics.title: Agent MoE Experiment: MLA q_lora_rank=0 (direct Q projection) at d1024 + d2048
topics.body:
Does MLA need the compressed Q latent, or is a direct Q projection (DeepSeek-V3 `q_lora_rank=0`) as good/better? Tested at d1024 and d2048. Per `experiments/grug/moe/ablation_runbook.md`.

**Pure-config ablation** — no code change. Run from `grug/moe-ablations` @ `a6d7c79ed2` via the existing `SCALE_Q_LORA_RANK` knob.

## Verbatim prompt

> Lets follow ablation doc and test q lora rank = 0 at d1024 and d2048.

## Variable under test

`SCALE_Q_LORA_RANK=0`. The MLA baseline routes Q through a compressed latent (`q_lora_rank = hidden/2` → `w_dq` [D,C_q] → `q_norm` → `w_uq` [C_q, N·qk]). Setting it to 0 uses a **single direct Q projection** `w_q` [D, N·qk] (the DeepSeek-V3 / TorchTitan default) — no Q latent, no `q_norm`. KV latent is unchanged. CPU-verified: `q_lora_rank=0` selects the direct-Q init branch (builds `w_q`, `w_dq`/`q_norm`/`w_uq` = None).

| size | baseline q_lora_rank | ablation |
|---|---|---|
| d1024 | 512 (hidden/2) | **0** (direct Q) |
| d2048 | 1024 (hidden/2) | **0** (direct Q) |

## Config (runbook + MLA)

MLA baseline (gate off, qk_mult 1.0, latent-dim corrections on, heads=hidden/128 via `SCALE_MLA_HEAD_MULT=1`, qk 192), all-global (`SCALE_SLIDING_WINDOW=4096`), datakit 2-phase, evals on, s3, MuonH heuristic. Only `SCALE_Q_LORA_RANK=0` differs from the MLA baseline.

- **d1024:** 12 layers · 128 experts top-4 · batch 256 · 4768 steps · **4× B200**
- **d2048:** 24 layers · 128 experts top-4 · batch 1024 · 11921 steps · **16× B200**

## Runs

| size | run id |
|---|---|
| d1024 | `gb200-d1024-mla-qlora0` |
| d2048 | `gb200-d2048-mla-qlora0` |

Baselines (q_lora_rank hidden/2): `gb200-d1024-mla-global-lr-base-v2`, and the d2048 MLA baseline.

```bash
# d1024 (d2048: SCALE_GPU_REPLICAS 4, SCALE_HIDDEN_DIM 2048, SCALE_NUM_LAYERS 24, SCALE_BATCH 1024, SCALE_STEPS 11921)
iris --cluster=marin job run --no-wait --enable-extra-resources \
  --target-cluster cw-us-east-08a --priority interactive \
  --cpu 2 --memory 8GB --disk 32GB --timeout 21600 --job-name gb200-d1024-mla-qlora0-coord \
  -e SCALE_GPUS_PER_NODE 4 -e SCALE_GPU_TYPE GB200 -e SCALE_GPU_REPLICAS 1 -e SCALE_EXPERT_AXIS 1 -e SCALE_REPLICA_AXIS 1 \
  -e SCALE_HIDDEN_DIM 1024 -e SCALE_NUM_LAYERS 12 -e SCALE_NUM_EXPERTS 128 -e SCALE_NUM_KV_HEADS 2 -e SCALE_TOP_K 4 \
  -e SCALE_MLA 1 -e SCALE_MLA_HEAD_MULT 1 -e SCALE_Q_LORA_RANK 0 \
  -e SCALE_SEQ_LEN 4096 -e SCALE_BATCH 256 -e SCALE_STEPS 4768 -e SCALE_SLIDING_WINDOW 4096 \
  -e SCALE_OPTIMIZER muonh -e SCALE_DATA datakit -e SCALE_EVAL 1 \
  -e SCALE_ATTN_IMPL gpu_fa4_cute -e SCALE_MOE_IMPL sonic_cute -e SCALE_SCAN_LAYERS 1 \
  -e SCALE_MUON_DIST_NONEXPERT 1 -e SCALE_MUON_INTRA_RACK 1 -e SCALE_MUON_PAD_NONEXPERT 1 -e SCALE_MUON_SYRK 1 \
  -e CE_IMPL liger -e CE_LIGER_CHUNK 8192 -e SCALE_REMAT recompute_all -e XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR cuda_async \
  -e SCALE_TRACKER wandb -e WANDB_API_KEY "$WANDB_API_KEY" -e WANDB_PROJECT marin_moe -e SCALE_CHECKPOINTS s3 \

topics.title: [levanter] Invert the GDN chunk operator by blockwise doubling
topics.body:
chunk_gated_delta_rule computed T = (I - A)^{-1} for each chunk with a C-step lax.fori_loop that rewrote one row per step. Replace it with unit_lower_triangular_inverse, which merges inverted diagonal blocks pairwise from 1x1 up to C x C:

```
inv([[I - A11, 0], [-A21, I - A22]]) = [[T11, 0], [T22 A21 T11, T22]]
```

Each of the log2(C) levels is two batched matmuls, and non-power-of-two chunk sizes are zero-padded. flash-linear-attention's solve_tril uses the same blocked scheme from a 16x16 base. The matmuls use Precision.HIGHEST to keep the fp32 arithmetic of the loop.

Reverse-mode AD through the loop stored the whole (B, H, Nc, C, C) operator at every row step. At B=4, H=8, L=8192, d_k=d_v=128, XLA's compiled temp memory for forward+backward falls from 7.0 to 3.2 GiB at C=64 and from 19.3 to 3.7 GiB at C=128 (memory_analysis of the CPU compile).

Median of 20 jitted chunk_gated_delta_rule runs at that shape, fp32 inputs, jax 0.11.1, in ms (loop → blocked):

| device | C | forward | forward+backward |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| H100 | 64 | 7.6 → 5.4 | 34.2 → 19.7 |
| H100 | 128 | 11.8 → 4.8 | 70.3 → 15.9 |
| B200 | 64 | 5.5 → 4.4 | 27.1 → 17.1 |
| B200 | 128 | 7.9 → 3.2 | 49.2 → 11.6 |

With bf16 inputs, as under Marin's params=float32,compute=bfloat16 policy, forward+backward at C=64 falls from 33.3 to 18.9 ms on H100 and from 27.5 to 17.3 ms on B200. At C=128 it falls from 69.2 to 15.2 ms and from 49.8 to 11.7 ms. The kernel casts its inputs to fp32, so the speedups match the fp32 runs.

TPU performance was not measured.

On H100 with gates g <= 0 and every matmul at "highest" precision, outputs match the loop version to 1.1e-7 relative. At default GPU matmul precision both versions differ from that reference by the same 8.3e-4 relative, which comes from the TF32 einsums after the solve.

The KDA prototype for #7291 computes the same inverse with a log-depth Neumann product.

topics.title: [grug] Flatten MLP tokens locally under context parallelism
topics.body:
The shared and routed MLPs now flatten `[B, S, D]` into tokens inside a `shard_map`. Each device flattens its own block of rows and sequence shard, so no data moves between devices. `_unflatten_tokens` reverses the flatten and restores the residual layout.

The old flatten used a global `(b s)` rearrange. Under context parallelism with more than one row per batch shard, it needed an all-to-all each way in every layer. Without context sharding, the token order does not change. With it, each expert-parallel group gets one sequence slice of each row instead of whole rows. This changes which tokens a full expert drops.

A CPU test checks that CP2 logits equal CP1 logits when no token drops. The compiled CP2 forward has 4 all-to-alls instead of 8.

On one GB200 rack at 65K context on CP4/EP16, restored from hero step 240000 (106 steps per arm):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| step time | 15.938 s | 15.586 s (+2.26% tokens/s) |
| drop fraction | 1.17% | 0.23% |
| loss | | −2.3e-3 |

With #10121, CP4 takes 14.626 s per step against 15.137 s and 1.94% drops on CP1. At 262K on CP4/EP16, each device holds one row, so the compiled program does not change.

comments.body:
🤖 Archived the description before automated prose cleanup.
<!-- marin-prose-cleanup-archive:b5089f579a6e1aeff26575db225c1143dba41cf3809bd78bd75283ed47114b86 -->

<details><summary>Original description</summary>

```markdown
The hero's shared and routed MLPs now flatten `[B, S, D]` into tokens locally on each device instead of with a global `(b s)` rearrange. With the sequence sharded over context, the global rearrange is an all-to-all in each direction, forward and backward, in every layer. Without context sharding nothing changes: each device already holds whole rows, so the local and global token orders are the same.

`_flatten_tokens` reshapes each device's block of rows and sequence shard in a `shard_map`, and `_unflatten_tokens` inverts it and restores the residual layout. Under context parallelism the experts then see tokens shard-major. Routing is per token, so the only order-dependent effect is which tokens a full expert drops first. A CPU test checks that CP2 logits equal CP1 logits on the same parameters when no token drops; the compiled CP2 forward goes from 8 all-to-alls to the 4 of the expert transport.

On one GB200 NVL72 rack restored from hero step 240000 at 65K context on CP4/EP16, on top of #10121's row balancing (same rack, 106 scored steps per arm), step time goes from 15.035 to 14.626 s (+2.80% tokens/s). The drop fraction falls from 2.21% to 0.23% and loss is 4.2e-3 lower. The old flatten gave each expert-parallel group 16 whole 65K rows, so a single-document row put a sixteenth of the group's tokens on one document's preferred experts; the local flatten splits that document across the four groups and mixes slices of all 64 rows into each. The same configuration on CP1 runs at 15.137 s with 1.94% drops, so with this change CP4 is the faster and more faithful 65K layout.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01V7n2oqJz61dkhYLBwNWYj9

```

</details>

topics.title: [data] Add content-preserving structure closure probes
topics.body:
Build deterministic closure probes from BFCL reference answers selected by the supplied cohort and split manifests across JSON objects, arrays, nesting, escapes, tool delimiters, reasoning delimiters, and code fences. Continuation controls distinguish closing a structure from dropping required content. Train and validation parent IDs remain disjoint.

Prepare prefix-preserving token targets, native-format tool probes, and evaluation audits that separate syntax validity from content-preserving success. Missing or unverified responses invalidate a complete audit. These are synthetic conditional-completion probes; they do not establish free-generation or downstream-task improvement.

The port contains dataset builders and audit tools. Historical run launchers and storage locators remain on #10190.

Part of #10305.

topics.title: [taskforge] Add the TaskProposal document and proposal sources
topics.body:
Add `stage10_proposal`. A `TaskProposal` is strictly validated YAML front matter plus a markdown body with the required section headings. `parse` and `render` round-trip it, `digest` hashes the canonical bytes, and `document_regex` constrains a completion to that canonical layout. `parse` also checks the research decision against the listed research items. `stage10_proposal.source` defines `ProposalBatch`, its slots, and the `ProposalSource` protocol.

`solver_machine` pins the solver's machine in the proposal: `null` for a container proposal, which runs in the image its build publishes, or one of `none`, `shellsim`, `cpython` and `packages` otherwise, with `none` legal only for a reasoning proposal. The proposer or triage writes it, and the build refuses a task whose machine differs from it (#10298), so no revision can move the solver between machines.

Builds on #10294; #10296 builds on it. The taskforge suite passes 365 tests here (43 more than #10294).

topics.title: Add the Smartie joint-domain RL campaign
topics.body:
Add the Smartie campaign for joint training on structural closure, competitive coding, SWE-smith, NL2Bash, TaskForge and CalibForge tasks. Version the admitted data, fixed validation panels and saved training configurations. New runtime revisions use fresh run identities; submitted configurations remain immutable.

Pin MarinSkyRL to eedfec34799dd35ba3e19733d9e70efedc4730e1, which includes concurrent native/Harbor evaluation and benchmark task caching. The continuation starts from run 2026.10.15.32 step 14, the best surviving checkpoint by recorded inline validation score, shuffles training data, retains ten checkpoints, and uses 112 H100s. Run 2026.10.16.43 finished its initial validation pass with 621 of 663 attempted tasks graded; optimizer updates and post-update validation remain unverified. Before merging this PR, repin to the merged runtime repair commits on MarinSkyRL main, including [#1019](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/1019).

RolloutEngine accepts an explicit remote judge connection, propagates caller cancellation during cleanup, and checks replay prefixes after history transitions. Preserve grading after a conversation reset or an abandoned completion request; exclude undelivered responses from training records. RL coordinators reject missing declared secrets, and colocated SkyRL jobs reject expert-block weight synchronization. Local Shellbox execution rejects non-Linux hosts; curation image builds enforce tracked inputs only inside Git worktrees.

Offline closure audits reuse Verifyit's training scorer, including typed JSON comparison and signed-zero equality. Parsing accepts a numeric JSON scalar before a tool delimiter; structural content rewards still require the expected object. Marin's test environment includes RolloutEngine and the Daytona backend.

[Evaluation design](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10043#issuecomment-6214235547). Part of #10043.

topics.title: [grug] Read precomputed fa4_bounds in the AMD Pallas flash kernel
topics.body:
`moe_hero_ep`, `moe_hero_fsdp` and `fast_track` run their layers in one homogeneous `lax.scan` and pick each layer's sliding window by selecting between precomputed `fa4_bounds` arrays (`experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py:1338-1359`). They have to: the window is a static `AttentionMask` field that the scan body cannot vary. `gpu_pallas_triton_flash` rejected any mask that carried those bounds, so none of these models could run on AMD GPUs with it. The kernel now uses the bounds as its per-query key lower bounds, as `gpu_fa4_cute` does.

A padding query (`valid=False`) attends only to itself, so outputs differ from the segment-ID path only on padding rows, which the loss masks. The kernels trust the bounds: after padding rows are set to their own position, the bounds must be nondecreasing and at most each query's position, which `fa4_cute_segment_bounds` gives when every segment ID is one contiguous run. The dK/dV pass depends on that ordering, so arbitrary bounds give wrong key and value gradients without raising. The module docstring and the `AttentionMask.fa4_bounds` comment state this.

The tests compare the bounds path with the segment-ID path at full causal and window 40 to 1e-6, and run the `moe_hero_ep` pattern against the reference on a 2x2 data/model mesh: long and short bounds computed outside a `lax.scan`, sharded over the batch, and selected per layer with `jnp.where`. The one-device Grug mesh test also runs through the bounds path, where the bounds, like q, name length-1 Explicit axes. A GPU-only test covers bf16 at the default tile sizes, 4096 tokens and window 2048.

Part of #9812

Long and short bounds are computed outside a `lax.scan`, sharded over the batch, and selected per layer with `jnp.where`. - bf16 at production settings (93bf041b5a): a GPU-only test runs the bounds path in bf16 at the default tile sizes, 4096 tokens and window 2048, against the reference. It is skipped in the CPU interpreter. An MI350X run of the full test file is queued on the AMD cluster, and I will post the result here.
- Bounds contract (93bf041b5a, 470be30b3c): the kernel module docstring, the `_key_lower_bounds` comment and the `AttentionMask.fa4_bounds` comment now spell out the requirement. After invalid rows are set to their own position, the bounds must be nondecreasing and at most each query's position. `fa4_cute_segment_bounds` produces such bounds when every segment ID, padding included, is one contiguous run. topics.title: [eval] Recover brokered evaluations after inference preemption
topics.body:
Use the existing inference broker for single-instance evaluations, with streaming responses and worker readiness. Requests keep a stable endpoint when GPU workers move. Pipeline-parallel gangs retain direct serving.

When model or judge inference is unavailable, stop the evaluator, wait outside the harness, and resume committed work after readiness returns. Completed StepSpecs stay cached. Advance Evalchemy to 09d27c93 so saved transport failures are retried without discarding completed responses.

Stream responses can be replayed only before the broker accepts response headers from the worker. Later worker loss breaks the stream. Buffers are bounded and abandoned requests are canceled. The broker's in-memory queue is not durable across broker actor failure.

Uses the existing broker instead of the separate relay proposed in #10033.

Fixes #10030.

🤖 Holistic review of e7b8dcb8e8f2a67e7ba8e7d17fdac56b4a11a128.

The PR moves inference-outage handling from the Harbor runner into a shared `run_with_inference_recovery` loop. Harbor and Evalchemy now stop their child work, wait for the backends, and resume against the same output directory. The shared loop fits the existing `EvalExecutor` seam, and the changed unit tests pass locally. One consequence of the transport-failure rejection needs an operator path, and one write is redundant. #10033 is a competing fix for the same failure and should be reconciled before either PR lands.

**Should fix**
1. `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/runner.py:426` `resuming_archive` is true for any non-empty archive at `output_dir`, not only for archives this process interrupted. `run_served_evalchemy` uses the step's deterministic `out_path` (`experiment/evaluation.py:77-79`), and StepRunner or orchestrator retries reuse it. Suppose a first attempt saved even one transport failure that the fresh-attempt branch at :437 and the coverage gate at :505-514 accepted. Every later rerun of that step then fails as `INFRA_FAILED`, and no retry can clear it. The message at :440 does not name the archive or say what an operator must do. Put `output_dir` and the remedy (delete the archive to rerun) in the `EvaluationError` message. Add the same sentence to the README paragraph that this PR adds, so the permanent failure has a documented exit.
2. `lib/marin/src/marin/experiment/evaluation.py:117` `write_artifact(result.result_payload(), output_dir)` duplicates the record write in `_lower`'s step fn (`lib/marin/src/marin/execution/lazy.py:376-388`). That fn writes the full `ArtifactRecord` at the same path from `result.result_payload()` after `run_served_evalchemy` returns. Since `FineStoreEvalchemyResult` now carries `jobs`, the step record already persists them. The manual write adds a window in which a minimal record exists with no name, version, fingerprint, or provenance. Delete line 117 and the `write_artifact` import at :37.
3. `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/result.py:58` and `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py:201,262` The docstring rewrites are unrelated to preemption recovery, and they remove invariants that the code still depends on. `EvalchemyResult` lost the note that historical reports persist its type name, so the class is part of the durable decoding contract; without it, the class reads as deletable. `_attempted_trials` lost the reason it returns `None` rather than the number of trials found: a found count would certify an interrupted run as complete. `_aggregate` lost the reason it divides by scored trials. Restore those three docstrings, or move these hunks to their own PR.

**Related PRs**
4. #10033: competing fix for the same incident (Evalchemy losing a re-registered serve). It rewrites the same `_run_evalchemy_child` wait loop and signature (`model` → `session`, a `_wait_while_serving` loop) and edits `experiment/evaluation.py`, so the two PRs conflict textually. They also overlap in design: #10033 follows re-registration through a loopback relay, while this PR cancels the child and resumes it. Choose one owner for Evalchemy recovery. If this PR lands first, reduce #10033 to the Iris `endpoint_relay` and drop its Evalchemy runner hunks.
5. #9813: makes each evaluation a StepSpec, with StepRunner owning retries at each result path, and edits `evaluation/runner.py` and `experiments/evaluation/README.md`. Those StepRunner retries hit item 1 on every evaluation that saved a transport failure. Land this PR first; #9813 then needs to handle the permanent `INFRA_FAILED` from item 1 when it rebases.

<!-- marin-holistic-review:e7b8dcb8e8f2a67e7ba8e7d17fdac56b4a11a128 -->

🤖 Removed the three terse docstring rewrites and restored the Evalchemy type-name, Harbor trial-count, and scored-trial invariants. Affected tests (45) and changed-files lint passed.

<!-- marin-deslop:e7b8dcb8e8f2a67e7ba8e7d17fdac56b4a11a128 -->

🤖 Fixed items 1–3 in 298a9cdd44. The transport-failure error names the archive and explains how to regenerate its requests; the README gives the same instructions. Removed the partial artifact write. The regression now runs through a remote ArtifactStep and reloads the full record, including child job IDs, name, and version. The three docstrings retain their decoding and coverage invariants.

Merged main and resolved the #9813 conflicts. Recovery stays inside each evaluation's StepSpec lock, completed steps remain cached, and concurrent evaluators still omit server-wide metrics. All 201 targeted tests pass; lint and type checks pass.

#10033 remains open on another author's branch. This PR owns evaluator cancellation/resume; #10033 can retain its Iris relay, but its overlapping Evalchemy integration needs to be removed or reconciled before both land. That branch is unchanged here.

🤖 Isolated the recovery tests' sleep stub in 0f635aefaa. Patching Python's shared `time.sleep` made StepRunner's polling loops busy-wait. The affected case now takes 4.0 seconds locally (49.8 before). All 201 evaluation/recovery tests pass; awaiting CI. No production logic or deadlines changed.

topics.title: [Post-training][RLVR] Smartie: Multi-Domain RLVR Revisited on Snowball 67B A2B
topics.body:
## TL;DR

Smartie revisited multi-domain reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) on Snowball, a 67B-total / approximately 2B-active-parameter model. Run `2026.10.15.32` produced the checkpoint released as [Marin Snowball 67B-A2B v0.1](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1). At its released update 14, recorded native validation pass@1 rose from **41.21% to 50.22%**. NVIDIA task mean reward rose from **40.59% to 55.50%**, while structural-task mean reward fell from **39.09% to 32.92%**. The experiment shows useful task learning and recorded structural regression. It does not establish successful balanced joint optimization.

The intended mixture combined four domains from [NVIDIA Nemotron-RL-Ultra-Training-Blends](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-RL-Ultra-Training-Blends): calendar reasoning, competitive coding, Reasoning Gym puzzles, and STEM multiple-choice questions. These are called the NVIDIA cohort below. Synthetic structural-compliance tasks formed the other cohort. A configuration error left shuffling disabled: domain-grouped NVIDIA rows preceded the structural rows. The training-reward spike near update 16 therefore cannot be interpreted as a sudden general capability gain. The fixed-validation curves are the evidence used here.

## Setup

The run started from [Grug Merge Campaign2 DARE-TIES-02](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign2-DARE-TIES-02-2026.10.10/tree/153f5369f69a0c0a7203779099ec94e98c66748f), with a fresh optimizer. It did **not** start from the separately released Marin Snowball v0, which is a Campaign3 merge. [The model provenance report](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14#provenance-report) records the initializer's merge parents.

Training used asynchronous RLOO-N, a leave-one-out policy-gradient estimator with neutral treatment of masked infrastructure failures, and truncated importance sampling. The learning rate was `4e-6`, with 512 accepted prompt groups and 16 responses per group per update. The run used 64 H100 policy GPUs and 48 separate inference GPUs. There was no KL, entropy, or auxiliary FTPO loss; structural tasks used the same verifiable-reward objective as other tasks. Loss reduction was token-mean. The [exact submitted launch config, resolved config, and source patch](https://gist.github.com/penfever/40f0f81dd4fba022697e4fa5aeabb91d/b79646603c23bd466969ff498661a0e313b1024a) are public.

The N means neutral: a masked infrastructure-failure sample gets zero advantage and is excluded from other samples' leave-one-out baselines. Model failures can remain zero-reward samples in the baseline. A group contains responses to the same prompt; 512 accepted groups is the optimizer-batch target, not 512 arbitrary completed responses. The configuration requires at least four baseline-eligible responses per group; fully masked, stale, undersized, or contract-invalid groups cannot contribute normally, and constant-reward groups provide no relative learning signal. Exact accepted groups and valid loss-token shares per domain were not reconstructed. File row proportions must not be treated as optimizer exposure.

The [exact public data release](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-Data/tree/cb728a7636caad3fc6fa6b6ba85a49194d9d69a3) contains 69,487 training tasks and 910 native validation tasks. Training rows comprise 741 calendar, 7,553 competitive-coding, 1,918 Reasoning Gym, 1,911 STEM, and 57,364 structural tasks. These are task inputs for online generation, not a static collection of model answers. Structural families cover JSON objects, arrays, nesting and string escapes, code fences, reasoning delimiters, tool-call delimiters, and repeated-opener retention. A continuation task can ask the model to finish a supplied JSON prefix without adding fields or changing reference content. Valid syntax alone does not pass that content-preservation check.

## Results and limits

| Fixed native validation measure | Initializer, update 0 | Released update 14 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Combined recorded pass@1, 910 tasks (%) | 41.21 | 50.22 |
| NVIDIA mean outcome reward, 667 tasks (%) | 40.59 | 55.50 |
| Structural mean outcome reward, 243 tasks (%) | 39.09 | 32.92 |

Grading coverage was 654/667 NVIDIA tasks and 235/243 structural tasks at initialization, versus 667/667 and 226/243 at update 14. Structural mean among graded tasks also fell, from 40.43% to 35.40%, so missing grades do not fully explain the recorded structural regression.

Each validation task has one sampled response. Mean outcome reward averages per-task rewards in `[0,1]`; missing grades remain zero outcomes in the fixed denominator. The combined native metric is task-count weighted, not an equal average of source means. The runtime's recorded pass@1 uses an explicit pass verdict when available and otherwise positive reward; partial-credit tasks can count as passing. Reasoning Gym exhibits this distinction: its initial mean reward is 76.48%, while recorded pass@1 is 82.04%. Mean outcome reward and pass@1 are therefore different measures. These repeatedly inspected development results are not an independent final test or a statistical-significance claim.

Update 12 had the highest recorded native pass@1, **50.33%**, but its weights had already been removed by checkpoint retention. Update 14 was the best surviving checkpoint, at **50.22%**, and was exported with that limitation recorded. The [complete public W&B metric archive](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-Artifacts/tree/20a22f8a7bdcbca7edf38279b7c24d22826693a3/wandb-full-20261019) covers 22 returned history rows: the pre-training row 0 and recorded optimizer steps 1–21, with native validation through step 20. This does not establish whether an additional unlogged update occurred before cancellation.

The separate in-line BFCL-Parity, SWE-bench Verified, and OpenThoughts-TBLite panel suffered execution failures. Its incomplete results were not used as valid zero-accuracy benchmark measurements. A later independent release-policy evaluation and baseline comparison is published in [#10283](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10283); it is separate from the native validation curves in this report.

Later campaign runs tested shuffled mixtures, Harbor-native Mini-SWE-Agent execution, task-source repairs, and staged SWE-Smith repository setup. They do not contribute weights to the Step14 release. The active `.57` job is deliberately left running; its later results will be reported separately. This issue closes the historical publication record, not that live job.

## Reproducibility and conclusion

The release includes public weights, exact Step14 training/native-validation Parquets, launch configs, frozen metric history, figure inputs, and source revisions in the [campaign artifact archive](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026/tree/9f01d8146fc48d7c5eb9c95d08d46d86b81c0f66). The archive's [reproduction guide](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026/blob/9f01d8146fc48d7c5eb9c95d08d46d86b81c0f66/REPRODUCING.md) collects the historical revisions, submitted patch/config, input mapping, and original launch command. Code is recorded in [Marin #10190](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10190), [MarinSkyRL #1030](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/1030), and [Harbor #277](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/277). These are code-publication links, not claims that the PRs have merged. Historical reproduction uses the submitted source pins. Marin's latest-main RolloutEngine API integration remains pending in its draft PR; the two runtime fork worktrees were refreshed against main.

Existing private repositories remain private. Raw conversations, restricted TaskForge inputs, uncleared third-party task assets, secrets, and transient environments are excluded from this public artifact upload. Those exclusions limit independent reconstruction of later restricted-data runs and trace-level failure analyses. The original Megatron optimizer checkpoint and a complete raw rollout history are not included, so bitwise training or export reproduction is not claimed.

The main next experiment is shuffled joint exposure with measured per-domain optimizer admission and valid-token contribution. A separate comparison can test sequence-mean loss to reduce response-length weighting. Structural retention needs an explicit checkpoint-selection constraint. Agentic benchmark claims require complete, graded benchmark cohorts; a training-reward increase alone is insufficient.

The real/structural mean-reward columns use the tracker's graded-only convention and may differ from the fixed-denominator means in the release figure. `Real` denotes the four NVIDIA domains in `.32`, but later runs change the cohort. `Recorded optimizer step` is the run's counter, separate from initializer ancestry; it can reset with a fresh optimizer and continue across a training-state resume. @ravwojdyla FYI this issue contains the experiment that produced v0.1

🤖 Update: Smartie `2026.10.19.57` completed 12 recorded optimizer updates and was stopped on October 20 after later agentic validation scores declined. [Update 8 is exported publicly](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.19.57-step8). This is an experimental continuation; it does not replace the earlier Marin Snowball v0.1 release.

The initializer was [Smartie `.32` update 14](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14), with a fresh optimizer. The run used asynchronous RLOO-N, a configured training batch of 512 groups × 16 responses per update, AdamW at `4e-6`, token-mean loss, and no KL or entropy auxiliary loss. [W&B](https://wandb.ai/dogml/snowball-smartie-rl/runs/v1vksnkr).

### Per-domain results and artifacts

The [public artifact bundle](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/e0d611e5e5d10ce2ba7b1f807e3a8a/runs/2026.10.19.57/update-20261020) contains PNG/SVG figures, CSV/JSON plot values, selected numeric W&B metrics, plotting code, the launch configuration, and exact data links.

![Per-domain validation reward](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/e0d611e5e5d10ce2ba7b1f807e3a8a/runs/2026.10.19.57/update-20261020/per-domain-validation-reward.png)

All values below are mean verifier scores among graded attempts, scaled to percent. Scores can include partial credit, so these are not uniformly binary success rates. They differ from fixed-denominator averages in some earlier campaign figures. These are repeatedly inspected development panels with one sampled response per task, not full release-policy evaluations. [Exact graded/attempted counts for every domain and checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026/blob/6662745944e0d611e5e5d10ce2ba7b1f807e3a8a/runs/2026.10.19.57/update-20261020/validation-curves.csv).

| Validation domain | Initializer | Update 8 | Update 12 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SWE-Smith full issue repair | 27.16 | 34.34 | 9.78 |
| CalibForge | - | - | - |
| NL2Bash | 71.00 | 57.58 | 27.00 |
| Competitive coding | 51.28 | 45.07 | 26.87 |
| Structural compliance | 36.36 | 63.20 | 76.09 |
| TaskForge | 72.88 | 6.26 | 0.88 |
| SWE-bench Verified, Terminus-2 | 3.33 | 33.33 | 6.67 |
| BFCL-Parity, Terminus-2 | 53.33 | 66.67 | 13.33 |
| OT-TBLite, Terminus-2 | 6.90 | 13.33 | 0.00 |

CalibForge has no valid grades: all four tasks fail agent startup at every checkpoint. SWE-Smith grade coverage is 81/100, 99/100, and 92/100 at the three tabulated checkpoints. The decline also holds on the same 64 SWE-Smith tasks graded at all seven evaluations (updates 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12): 28.13% initially, 42.19% at update 8, and 14.06% at update 12. Update 8 was selected for export by the user; it is not uniformly best across domains.

![Validation grading coverage](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/e0d611e5e5d10ce2ba7b1f807e3a8a/runs/2026.10.19.57/update-20261020/validation-coverage.png)

### Training mix and exact data

Training used 3,322 rows: **1,661 SWE-Smith Stage 1 repository-setup tasks and 1,661 structural tasks**, with shuffle enabled. Stage 1 asks the agent to prepare the correct repository, branch, commit, and installation; it does not ask for a bug fix. SWE-Smith validation still tests full issue repair. CalibForge and the other domains above are validation-only in this run.

![Training-source reward](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/e0d611e5e5d10ce2ba7b1f807e3a8a/runs/2026.10.19.57/update-20261020/training-source-reward.png)

- [Exact training Parquet](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove-smartie-continuation-private/blob/3cd8b45655637b5d1b79ca607d007537706e2981/releases/2026.10.19.1/stage1-structural-mixture/train.parquet).
- [Exact 573-row validation Parquet](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove-smartie-continuation-private/blob/3cd8b45655637b5d1b79ca607d007537706e2981/releases/2026.10.19.1/stage1-structural-mixture/validation.parquet).
- [Source-owned agent profile and task requirements](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove-smartie-continuation-private/blob/3cd8b45655637b5d1b79ca607d007537706e2981/releases/2026.10.19.1/stage1-structural-mixture/README.md).
- [Launch config](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/e0d611e5e5d10ce2ba7b1f807e3a8a/runs/2026.10.19.57/update-20261020/training-launch.yaml) and [data hashes/provenance](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/e0d611e5e5d10ce2ba7b1f807e3a8a/runs/2026.10.19.57/update-20261020/data-provenance.json).

The exact data files remain **private and access-controlled**. Validation includes restricted TaskForge payloads, and the complete task bundle has not been cleared for public redistribution. Both Parquet hashes were verified against this pinned HF revision. Exact reproduction requires data access.

Validation used the same declared release, URI, and file as `.56`; the release README also records that rows were copied unchanged from the preceding cohort. The 573 rows comprise 100 SWE-Smith, 100 NL2Bash, four CalibForge, 85 coding, 41 TaskForge, and 243 structural tasks. Three additional panels of 30 tasks each (BFCL, SWE-bench, and OT-TBLite) are configured in the launch file.

### Interpretation and follow-up

Structural scores improved while later issue-repair and tool-use scores declined. Original Harbor traces from 30 SWE-bench and 30 BFCL tasks at each of updates 8 and 12 show increased parser-error fractions (73.99% to 87.62% for SWE-bench; 74.95% to 88.56% for BFCL). These evaluation traces were recovered independently of the training-trace publisher. A confirmed training-path defect clears earlier action tokens after history resets, leaving the final segment to receive whole-task reward. [Marin #10326](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10326) records the evidence and required TITO safeguards.

The defect's contribution to the reward decline has not been isolated experimentally. A separate trace-publisher failure limits late-run training evidence. The next training run needs verified preservation of all action segments and repaired trace retention before testing whether the narrow setup/structural mix itself harms broader behavior. No replacement run was launched as part of this update.

🤖 Data preservation follow-up: the campaign's staged SWE-Smith data and versioned RL inputs are archived in [the private campaign data archive](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove-smartie-continuation-private/tree/ab5173cc03cd4392d5b8cdf38a3392e1ff44a0bc/campaign-archive/2026.10.20): 84 archives, 179,190 data/evidence files plus a curation-code snapshot, about 5.8 GB compressed. Existing public releases remain public; this archive does not change their visibility.

Oracle solution execution was waived. |
| Repaired NL2Bash | [Public admitted release](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove/tree/772fd68384a511b9a2b8db9f2e397ae12ca0621e/releases/smartie-continuation-20261016/nl2bash) | 996 retained tasks; task payloads and quality decisions. Historical oracle-path fixes and splits are also in the private archive. |
| Repaired full SWE-Smith | [Public admitted release](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove/tree/0e8137a6a1eca1e2c8c12eeb90a16c5d7f1f750c/releases/smartie-continuation-20261016/swesmith) | 8,045 quality-admitted tasks. Historical filtering, split and oracle inputs are also in the private archive. |
| Other campaign RL data | [Archive manifest](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove-smartie-continuation-private/blob/ab5173cc03cd4392d5b8cdf38a3392e1ff44a0bc/campaign-archive/2026.10.20/manifest.json) | Structural datasets, mixed training/validation revisions, TaskForge inputs, source splits, admission decisions, and canary inputs. Private where redistribution review is incomplete or source access is restricted. |

Stage 3 was not used in run `.57`. Its 600 complete handoffs start from repaired code that passed the original required tests. Its 178 partial handoffs start from partially repaired code with a witnessed remaining test failure; the known repair passes those tests. All 30 representative runtime controls across six repositories returned expected grades, including rejection of protected-file corruption and injected passing tests. This does not establish 778 independent full agent runs. Original parent-task split assignments are preserved, but repositories overlap across splits.

Direct Stage 3 downloads: [train JSONL](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove-smartie-continuation-private/blob/ab5173cc03cd4392d5b8cdf38a3392e1ff44a0bc/campaign-archive/2026.10.20/stage3/train.jsonl), [validation JSONL](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove-smartie-continuation-private/blob/ab5173cc03cd4392d5b8cdf38a3392e1ff44a0bc/campaign-archive/2026.10.20/stage3/validation.jsonl), and [admission manifest](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove-smartie-continuation-private/blob/ab5173cc03cd4392d5b8cdf38a3392e1ff44a0bc/campaign-archive/2026.10.20/stage3/variants-manifest.json). These are private, byte-verified copies of the frozen exports.

Stage 3 still needs its local actor/verifier images rebuilt or separately distributed before another machine can execute it. Its image locators are local IDs, not pullable registry references. The archive includes the curation source snapshot, recorded image mappings, and task resources; it does not include local container image archives. Rebuilding from the archived material has not been tested on a fresh machine, so this is not a self-contained execution release. Keep private tests, gold solutions, and verifier resources outside model access.

“Quality-admitted” means the curation pipeline accepted a task; it is not a model-solving accuracy claim. CalibForge's environment admission checks cover fixture equivalence and setup/verifier execution, with oracle solution execution explicitly skipped. Its public v2 release includes train/validation splits. The public NL2Bash and full SWE-Smith releases contain task cohorts and review decisions; their campaign-specific splits are in the private archive. Private downloads require access to the Open-Athena repository.

The archive contains historical and rejected candidates as well as admitted data. Use each version's admission manifest rather than treating all archived rows as approved training examples. Raw source mirrors, mounted source volumes, caches, and operational log directories were excluded. The file manifest records SHA-256 hashes and exclusions; no archived dataset is silently relabeled as public or fully runnable.

The latest run's validation Parquet was also checked against the previous Stage 1 release: both have SHA-256 `5e851fd5376aca35f307b13d3d16b74414fcc8d9be7b4ab26b4c9e46b45a1c6c`. No validation-data change was introduced between those releases.

topics.title: [iris] GPU jobs default to NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and flood log forwarding
topics.body:
Every Iris job that requests a GPU extra gets `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` with `NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=INIT,BOOTSTRAP,ENV,NET,GRAPH,TUNING,RAS` from the default environment in `lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/types.py:779`. Marin's training launcher sets `NCCL_DEBUG` to `WARN` only when nothing is preset (`lib/marin/src/marin/training/training.py:418`, `setdefault`), so the Iris default wins for every training job.

On 2026-10-17 four 32-GPU SFT jobs (`/karan/task203-lr*`, cw-rno2a) emitted about 80,000 log lines per second, mostly `NCCL INFO` per-collective output, while log forwarding accepts about 34,500 lines per second; the hub fell about 90 minutes behind on that cluster's logs.

Reproduce: submit any GPU job without setting `NCCL_DEBUG` and read its task log; `NCCL INFO AllReduce: ... Algo TREE proto LL ...` lines appear for every collective.

Expected: GPU jobs default to `NCCL_DEBUG=WARN` (abort and transport errors remain visible), with INFO and the subsystem list set only by jobs that are debugging NCCL (for example the recovery or wedge repro experiments, which already set INFO explicitly).

Done when: the Iris GPU default is `WARN` without a subsystem list, Marin's training launcher no longer needs to guess, and the two call sites that want INFO set it themselves.
